summary_zh: 据报道，首席执行官与一名向北京传递信息的中国女商人关系密切，英伟达周日表示，“正在启动一项内部调查”。
body_en: CEO reportedly ‌had close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing
Nvidia said ⁠on Sunday it “is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”.

The Republican-led foreign affairs and intelligence committees of the US Congress asked Huang to testify next week at a closed-door briefing on Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage” in response to a New York Times report in ​October alleging he ‌had a close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing.

Alice Huang or Huang Le, of no relation to the Nvidia CEO, is an executive at a Singapore-based datacenter company called Megaspeed. She had previously been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, prompting American officials to surveil and monitor her.
Those officials have determined that she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times reported, citing unnamed sources.

The company’s board said in a statement on that, while it has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry will examine all available information.

“The Board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said. “The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.”
Huang fully ‌supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, it added.

Axios reported on ​Sunday, citing a draft email by Huang to employees, that Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and took full ⁠responsibility for his actions.
“I was unfaithful to my ​wife. My ​actions hurt her ​and our children. There is no excuse ​for what ‌I did,” ​Huang said ​in the draft email also seen by Reuters.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the Axios report.

The Times reported on Sunday that a memo drafted by US secretary of state Marco Rubio circulated among top policymakers in the Trump administration last spring, citing intelligence that the businesswoman who had a relationship with Nvidia’s chief executive was a spy for China’s ministry of state security. Despite those concerns, Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, were invited to a state dinner at the White House in September for Xi Jinping, China’s president, and seated at the top table with Donald Trump and Xi.

Nvidia’s powerful chips serve as a cornerstone of the AI boom, placing Jensen Huang into one of the most influential leadership positions in the industry. In that position, he has developed a close partnership with Trump as the US government attempts to defend its position as a leader in AI development.
However, national security concerns have prompted strict US export controls, effectively barring the company from selling its top-tier processors to customers in China.

US officials have cited threats to the US supply chain and fears over national security risks as a rationale for the restrictions. Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, has also suggested that China could be sanctioned for theft of US data and intellectual property.

The Trump administration has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China as a matter of national security. Megaspeed’s Alice Huang was suspected to have been helping the government get around those restrictions.

The investigation also follows a rough few days on Wall Street for AI tech firms, particularly Nvidia. A sell-off of tech stocks that began earlier this month and gained steam with disappointing earnings led to a total decline of nearly $1tn in value off the tech-heavy Nasdaq exchange in one week and erased about $2tn in a month.
A drop of 3.1% for Nvidia, previously worth about $5tn, whose chips have made it the poster child of the AI frenzy, was the heaviest force pulling the S&P 500 downward recently.
body_zh: 据报道，首席执行官与一名向北京传递信息的中国女商人关系密切
英伟达周日表示，“鉴于最近有报道称创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋已成为外国情报工作的目标，该公司正在启动独立调查”。
美国国会共和党领导的外交事务和情报委员会要求黄在下周的一次闭门简报会上就英伟达的“针对外国对手间谍活动的安全协议”作证，以回应《纽约时报》10 月份的一篇报道，称他与一名向北京传递信息的中国女商人关系密切。
Alice Huang 或 Huang Le 与 Nvidia 首席执行官没有关系，她是新加坡一家名为 Megaspeed 的数据中心公司的高管。她此前曾被怀疑向中国走私英伟达芯片，促使美国官员对她进行监视和监视。
据《纽约时报》援引未透露姓名的消息来源报道，这些官员已确定她充当中国情报人员，向北京传递商业信息。
该公司董事会在一份声明中表示，虽然没有理由相信美国国家安全或英伟达的机密遭到泄露，但其调查将检查所有可用信息。
该公司表示：“董事会优先考虑美国国家和经济安全，这对 NVIDIA 及其股东的利益至关重要。” “董事会对詹森和他的领导团队充满信心，并将酌情提供进一步的最新情况。”
声明补充说，黄完全支持审查并承诺与其合作。
Axios 周日报道称，黄向员工发送了一封电子邮件草稿，称黄承认与一名疑似中国间谍有恋爱关系，并对其行为承担全部责任。
“我对我的妻子不忠。我的行为伤害了她和我们的孩子。我的所作所为没有任何借口，”黄在路透社也看到的电子邮件草稿中说道。
Nvidia 没有立即回应对 Axios 报告发表评论的请求。
《泰晤士报》周日报道称，去年春天，美国国务卿马可·卢比奥起草的一份备忘录在特朗普政府高层政策制定者中流传，其中援引情报称，与英伟达首席执行官有关系的女商人是中国国家安全部的间谍。尽管存在这些担忧，黄和他的妻子洛丽·黄 (Lori Huang) 仍受邀参加 9 月份在白宫为中国国家主席习近平举行的国宴，并与唐纳德·特朗普和习近平一起坐在最高桌。
英伟达强大的芯片是人工智能热潮的基石，使黄仁勋成为业内最有影响力的领导职位之一。在这个职位上，随着美国政府试图捍卫其作为人工智能开发领导者的地位，他与特朗普建立了密切的合作伙伴关系。
然而，国家安全担忧促使美国实施严格的出口管制，实际上禁止该公司向中国客户出售其顶级处理器。
美国官员将对美国供应链的威胁和对国家安全风险的担忧作为实施限制的理由。美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特也表示，中国可能因窃取美国数据和知识产权而受到制裁。
出于国家安全考虑，特朗普政府对向中国出口先进人工智能芯片实施了限制。 Megaspeed 的 Alice Huang 被怀疑一直在帮助政府绕过这些限制。
此次调查之前，人工智能科技公司（尤其是英伟达）在华尔街经历了艰难的几天。本月早些时候开始的科技股抛售潮因令人失望的盈利而加剧，导致以科技股为主的纳斯达克交易所的市值在一周内下跌近 1 万亿美元，一个月内蒸发了约 2 万亿美元。
英伟达股价下跌 3.1%，此前市值约为 5 兆美元，该公司的芯片使其成为人工智能热潮的典型代表，是最近拉低标准普尔 500 指数的最大力量。

title_en: Trump and his Justice Department stand defiant as Democrats ready an investigative blitz
title_zh: 当民主党准备展开调查闪电战时，特朗普和他的司法部表现得目中无人
summary: President Donald Trump and his Department of Justice are taking a combative stance toward Democrats after their victories in the midterm elections
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统和他的司法部在中期选举中获胜后对民主党采取了好斗的立场
body_en: Election 2026 live updates: Trump says US took 'giant step back' through midterms
Blanche says 'there could be' investigations of Dems pushing oversight probes
Trump says US took 'giant step back' through midterm results
President Donald Trump and his Department of Justice are taking a combative stance toward Democrats after their victories in the midterm elections

President Donald Trump and his Department of Justice are taking a combative stance toward Democrats after their election victories in the midterms , signaling intense conflict to come as lawmakers prepare aggressive investigations into the executive branch next year.

Trump set the tone, declaring on social media that investigative requests already made by Democrats are “extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable.” Attorney General Todd Blanche echoed the Republican president and said criminal investigations of Democrats are possible.

“They are not allowed to just go around threatening existing members of the administration, to go around threatening companies, and that’s what President Trump is extremely worried about and he should be,” Blanche said as he and congressional Democrats appeared on the Sunday news shows to discuss the repercussions from last week's elections.

Rep. Robert Garcia, who is poised to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee in the next Congress, is preparing investigations into what he calls the “Trump crime family.” He said Democrats are not going to be intimidated.
“The days of us not fighting back are over,” said Garcia, D-Calif.

The early rhetoric sets up a showdown ahead that will likely define Trump’s remaining two years in office and test the power of Congress to put a check on the White House. About 7 in 10 voters nationally say Congress is not doing enough to provide checks and balances on the presidency, according to The AP Voter Poll , a survey of more than 100,000 midterm voters.
Democrats have made clear that impeachment is an option.

If there are people who have been "shortchanging the American people, screwing over the American people, or stealing from the American people, then they need to be held accountable in a manner consistent with Congress’ role, constitutionally,” said Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York.

But the investigative onslaught is also a source of tension for Democrats, with many warning that delivering on their central promise to voters — actions to lower the cost of living — must take precedence.
Some fear their resounding wins Tuesday that have given them healthy majorities in the House and Senate will prove fleeting if conflict with Trump defines the agenda .

Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton, the first Democrat elected to the chamber from Kansas in 94 years , expressed skepticism about impeachment, saying his campaign was about trying to bring people together. He said he does not want the next two years to be spent “dividing our country further.”

“I’m not as interested in impeachment as setting up guardrails,” Hamilton said. Still, Hamilton said he understands that some investigations are necessary, and Democrats “have to look at what’s happened in Washington.”
Sen. Bernie Sanders, a Vermont independent who caucuses with Democrats, said he wants to hold Trump accountable, but warned there was only so much time.
“We cannot spend all of our time investigating Trump," Sanders said. "We’ve got to stand up for working-class families, make a real difference in their lives.”

Jeffries, who is on the cusp of becoming the nation's first Black House speaker, was asked on election night about the prospects of working with Trump. He said he would be ready to work with the other side of the aisle “whenever and wherever possible to deliver real results.”
body_zh: 2026 年大选实时更新：特朗普称美国在中期选举中“大幅倒退”
布兰奇表示“可能”对民主党推动监督调查进行调查
特朗普称美国在中期选举结果中“大幅倒退”
唐纳德·特朗普总统和他的司法部在中期选举中获胜后对民主党采取了好斗的立场
唐纳德·特朗普总统和他的司法部在中期选举中获胜后对民主党采取了好斗的立场，这表明随着立法者准备明年对行政部门进行积极调查，激烈的冲突将会到来。
特朗普定下基调，在社交媒体上宣称民主党已经提出的调查要求是“最高层的敲诈勒索，他们应该承担责任”。司法部长托德·布兰奇呼应了共和党总统的说法，并表示对民主党人进行刑事调查是可能的。
布兰奇在与国会民主党人出现在周日新闻节目中讨论上周选举的影响时表示，“他们不被允许到处威胁现有的政府成员，到处威胁公司，这是特朗普总统非常担心的，也是他应该担心的。”
众议员罗伯特·加西亚（Robert Garcia）即将在下一届国会担任强大的众议院监督委员会主席，他正在准备对他所谓的“特朗普犯罪家族”进行调查。他说民主党不会被吓倒。
“我们不反击的日子已经结束了，”加利福尼亚州民主党人加西亚说。
早期的言论预示着一场摊牌可能会决定特朗普剩余两年的任期，并考验国会对白宫进行制衡的权力。美联社选民民意调查对超过 10 万中期选民进行了调查，结果显示，全国大约十分之七的选民表示，国会在对总统职位进行制衡方面做得不够。
民主党人已明确表示弹劾是一种选择。
纽约民主党众议院领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯表示，如果有人“欺骗美国人民，欺骗美国人民，或者偷窃美国人民的东西，那么他们就需要以符合国会角色和宪法的方式承担责任”。
但调查的猛烈攻击也是民主党人紧张的一个根源，许多人警告说，必须优先兑现他们对选民的核心承诺——降低生活成本的行动。
一些人担心，如果与特朗普的冲突决定了议程，他们周二在众议院和参议院获得的压倒性胜利将转瞬即逝。
当选参议员亚当·汉密尔顿 (Adam Hamilton) 是 94 年来首位从堪萨斯州当选众议院议员的民主党人，他对弹劾表示怀疑，称他的竞选活动是为了让人们团结在一起。他表示，他不希望未来两年“进一步分裂我们的国家”。
汉密尔顿说：“我对弹劾不如设置护栏感兴趣。”不过，汉密尔顿表示，他理解一些调查是必要的，民主党人“必须看看华盛顿发生了什么”。
与民主党一起参加党团会议的佛蒙特州无党派参议员伯尼·桑德斯表示，他希望让特朗普承担责任，但警告说时间有限。
“我们不能把所有时间都花在调查特朗普上，”桑德斯说。 “我们必须支持工薪阶层家庭，真正改变他们的生活。”
即将成为美国首位黑宫议长的杰弗里斯在选举之夜被问及与特朗普合作的前景。他表示，他愿意“随时随地”与另一方合作，以取得真正的成果。

title_en: The Kremlin hopes the U.S. election shake-up won't shift Trump's negotiations on Ukraine
title_zh: 克里姆林宫希望美国大选的变动不会改变特朗普的乌克兰谈判
summary: Asked if the election's outcome could stymie U.S. attempts to help negotiate a settlement between Moscow and Kyiv, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov voiced hope that President Donald Trump will continue to pursue his peace efforts.
summary_zh: 当被问及选举结果是否会阻碍美国帮助莫斯科和基辅之间谈判达成和解的努力时，克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫
body_en: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/the-kremlin-hopes-the-u-s-election-shake-up-wont-shift-trumps-negotiations-on-ukraine
World Updated on Nov 8, 2026 5:48 PM EST — Published on Nov 8, 2026 3:15 PM EST

The Republicans' defeat in the U.S. midterm elections was watched closely in Russia, where some observers are predicting it could herald more support for Ukraine when the Democrats take over Congress in January.
But if the Kremlin is hearing the ticking of a clock on its nearly 5-year-old full-scale invasion of its neighbor, it seemingly remains unperturbed.

Asked if the election's outcome could stymie U.S. attempts to help negotiate a settlement between Moscow and Kyiv, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov voiced hope that U.S. President Donald Trump will continue to pursue his peace efforts.

"There is groundwork already in place, and another round of trilateral negotiations is set to take place very soon," Peskov said of talks planned for Tuesday and Wednesday involving Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. representatives in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.

He also praised the "successful humanitarian peace-building efforts" by first lady Melania Trump, adding that "we hope that all of this will continue." Last week's limited ceasefire around the Russia-occupied city of Oleshky, brokered with her help, allowed for the delivery of humanitarian aid and the evacuation of some residents.
Peskov shrugged off a question from reporters on whether the new Congress would challenge Trump's stance on Russia and Ukraine. He called it an "internal matter" for the U.S.
Trump's recent moves have appeared to favor Moscow

Last month, he struck a diesel fuel import deal with Russia in a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on the Kremlin, to the dismay of Ukraine and its European allies. He also claimed that Kyiv's attacks on Russian oil refineries caused a spike in diesel prices in the U.S. He urged Kyiv to halt the strikes, even though rising global energy prices were largely driven by the Iran war.

Trump also issued an executive order to put on hold sweeping new sanctions that clamped down on the Russian economy, telling Congress the pause was in the national interest. Lawmakers from both parties blasted Trump's move as benefiting Russian President Vladimir Putin.

At the same time, Ukraine reported a throttling of Starshield, the military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX. Trump denied being behind the brief slowing of Starshield, but the move to limit the system that serves as the backbone of Ukraine's drone operations and battlefield communications was widely seen as part of Washington's efforts to pressure Kyiv.

The diesel deal appeared to falter this week after U.S. federal and state officials warned that handling any shipments could bring legal consequences, and two U.S.-bound tankers changed course. The Kremlin sought to play down the development, saying deliveries will continue.

Kyiv desperately needs to replenish its supplies of U.S.-made Patriot interceptors to fend off Russia's ballistic missile attacks. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made repeated requests for Washington to speed up delivery of the defensive systems, but U.S. stockpiles have been exhausted by the Iran war, and the U.S. has prioritized replenishing its own arsenals.
WATCH: Zelenskyy on his 'emotional' relationship with Trump and fighting Russia
On Oct. 30, the Trump administration said it has approved a proposed $2.1 billion sale of Patriot interceptors for Ukraine after Kyiv had accused the Pentagon of delaying delivery.
Trump also appeared to echo the Kremlin's view that Zelenskyy was an obstacle to peace while saying Putin was more open to a deal.

Trump on Thursday conferred with Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev, who attended a White House ceremony with the first lady recognizing last week's humanitarian truce. The president didn't meet any of the Ukrainian officials also at the event but hinted that some kind of grand deal about European security was in the works.
Dmitry Medvedev, who served as Russian president in 2008-12, predicted that Trump would be less inclined to press Ukraine when a new Congress is seated.
body_zh: 世界 更新于美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 8 日下午 5:48 — 发布于美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 8 日下午 3:15
共和党在美国中期选举中的失败受到俄罗斯的密切关注，一些观察家预测，当民主党一月份接管国会时，这可能预示着对乌克兰的更多支持。
但如果克里姆林宫听到其近五年来全面入侵邻国的时间即将过去，它似乎仍然泰然自若。
当被问及选举结果是否会阻碍美国帮助莫斯科和基辅之间通过谈判达成和解的努力时，克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫表示希望美国总统唐纳德·特朗普继续致力于和平努力。
佩斯科夫在谈到计划于周二和周三举行的、俄罗斯、乌克兰和美国代表在阿拉伯联合酋长国阿布扎比举行的会谈时表示，“基础工作已经到位，新一轮三边谈判很快就会进行。”
他还赞扬第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普“成功的人道主义和平建设努力”，并补充说“我们希望这一切能够继续下去”。上周在她的帮助下，俄罗斯占领的奥列什基市周围实现了有限停火，允许运送人道主义援助物资并疏散一些居民。
佩斯科夫对记者提出的新国会是否会挑战特朗普在俄罗斯和乌克兰问题上的立场的问题不屑一顾。他称这是美国的“内部事务”。
特朗普最近的举动似乎有利于莫斯科
上个月，他与俄罗斯达成了一项柴油进口协议，令人震惊地扭转了美国多年来对克里姆林宫施加的压力，令乌克兰及其欧洲盟友感到沮丧。他还声称基辅对俄罗斯炼油厂的袭击导致美国柴油价格飙升。他敦促基辅停止袭击，尽管全球能源价格上涨主要是由伊朗战争推动的。
特朗普还发布了一项行政命令，暂停对俄罗斯经济的全面新制裁，并告诉国会暂停符合国家利益。两党议员都谴责特朗普的举动有利于俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京。
与此同时，乌克兰报告称，Starshield 受到限制，Starshield 是埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 旗下 SpaceX 旗下 Starlink 卫星互联网服务的军用级版本。特朗普否认是星盾计划短暂放缓的幕后黑手，但限制该系统的举动被广泛视为华盛顿向基辅施压的一部分。该系统是乌克兰无人机行动和战场通信的支柱。
本周，在美国联邦和州官员警告称，处理任何货物都可能带来法律后果，并且两艘开往美国的油轮改变航线后，柴油交易似乎陷入困境。克里姆林宫试图淡化事态发展，表示将继续交付。
基辅迫切需要补充美国制造的爱国者拦截弹的供应，以抵御俄罗斯的弹道导弹袭击。乌克兰总统泽连斯基多次要求华盛顿加快交付防御系统，但美国的库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，美国已优先考虑补充自己的军火库。
观看：泽伦斯基谈论他与特朗普的“情感”关系以及与俄罗斯的斗争
10月30日，在基辅指责五角大楼推迟交付后，特朗普政府表示，已批准向乌克兰出售价值21亿美元的爱国者拦截弹的提议。
特朗普似乎也赞同克里姆林宫的观点，即泽连斯基是和平的障碍，同时表示普京对达成协议持更开放的态度。
特朗普周四与普京特使基里尔·德米特里耶夫进行了会谈，基里尔·德米特里耶夫出席了白宫仪式，第一夫人承认上周的人道主义休战。总统在此次活动中没有会见任何乌克兰官员，但暗示正在酝酿某种有关欧洲安全的重大协议。
2008-12 年担任俄罗斯总统的德米特里·梅德韦杰夫 (Dmitry Medvedev) 预测，当新一届国会就任后，特朗普将不太愿意向乌克兰施压。

title_en: Cruise ship pianist rescued after nine hours treading water miles from shore
title_zh: 游轮钢琴家在距离海岸几英里的地方踩水九小时后获救
summary: Man taken to hospital after falling off Royal Caribbean ship in Pacific Ocean, with Coast Guard investigating incident A pianist for a Royal Caribbean cruise ship is expected to survive after two Newport Beach, California , fishermen discovered him treading wa
summary_zh: 一名男子在太平洋从皇家加勒比游轮上坠落后被送往医院，海岸警卫队正在调查事件
body_en: Cruise ship pianist rescued after nine hours treading water miles from shore | California
Man taken to hospital after falling off Royal Caribbean ship in Pacific Ocean, with Coast Guard investigating incident

A pianist for a Royal Caribbean cruise ship is expected to survive after two Newport Beach, California , fishermen discovered him treading water in the Pacific Ocean nearly 20 miles (32km) offshore on Friday.
The unidentified man was taken to the hospital after the rescue, according to the US Coast Guard, which is now investigating how he went overboard from the cruise ship.

Authorities believe the man may have been in the ocean for approximately nine hours before he was spotted by Sean Norton and Grant Garrett, who were returning from a fishing trip near Catalina Island.
The two fishermen had spent the morning fishing for marlin when their trip took an unexpected turn. By noon, they had pulled the stranded man from the water.
“I’m like, ‘Yeah, it’s a human being. Stop the boat; let’s get all of our lines in,” Garrett told CBS News , recalling the moment the boat’s captain first saw the man in the water.

The fishermen quickly worked together to bring the man onboard. Once the man regained his composure, Garrett said he identified himself as a pianist onboard Royal Caribbean’s 14-deck cruise ship, the Ovation of the Seas.
According to Norton, the rescued crew member had few words to describe what he had just experienced. “The only thing he said to me was, ‘Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,’” Norton said.

After the rescue, the fishing crew issued an emergency maritime call, prompting Newport Beach lifeguards to respond and provide assistance. Battalion chief Adam Yacenda said the man was found approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, according to CBS, or “pretty much in the middle of the ocean”.
Despite the extended time spent in the water, Norton believes unusually warm ocean temperatures may have played a significant role in the man’s survival.
“You have this crazy super El Niño year. This guy was in the water for probably 10 hours, but the water’s 76 degrees,” Norton said. “A different year, no way he makes it.”

The circumstances surrounding the crew member’s fall from the cruise ship remain under investigation by the Coast Guard. Royal Caribbean Group acknowledged the incident and said it is assisting the employee following the ordeal.

In a statement to CBS, a company spokesperson said: “We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time. To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share.”
body_zh: 游轮上的钢琴家在距离海岸几英里的地方踩水九小时后获救加利福尼亚州
男子在太平洋从皇家加勒比游轮上坠落被送往医院，海岸警卫队正在调查事件
周五，加利福尼亚州纽波特海滩的两名渔民发现皇家加勒比游轮上的一名钢琴师在离岸近 20 英里（32 公里）的太平洋上踩水，预计他能生还。
据美国海岸警卫队称，这名身份不明的男子在获救后被送往医院，目前正在调查他是如何从游轮上落水的。
当局认为，这名男子可能在海里呆了大约九个小时，然后被肖恩·诺顿和格兰特·加勒特发现，他们当时正在卡塔利娜岛附近钓鱼回来。
两个渔民花了一个上午的时间去捕马林鱼，突然他们的行程发生了意外的转变。中午时分，他们将被困男子从水中救了出来。
“我想，‘是的，这是一个人。停下船；让我们把所有的绳索都收进去，’”加勒特告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，回忆起船长第一次看到水中那个人的那一刻。
渔民们迅速齐心协力，将男子带上船。当这名男子恢复镇静后，加勒特称自己是皇家加勒比 14 层甲板游轮“海洋赞礼号”上的一名钢琴家。
据诺顿说，获救的船员几乎无法用言语来描述他刚刚经历的事情。 “他对我说的唯一一句话就是，‘谢谢你。我以为我要死了，’”诺顿说。
救援结束后，渔船船员发出紧急海上呼叫，促使纽波特比奇救生员做出反应并提供援助。据哥伦比亚广播公司报道，营长亚当·亚森达 (Adam Yacenda) 表示，这名男子是在离岸约 15 至 20 英里的地方被发现的，或者说“几乎在大洋中央”。
尽管在水中度过了很长的时间，诺顿认为异常温暖的海洋温度可能对这名男子的生存起到了重要作用。
“今年发生了疯狂的超级厄尔尼诺现象。这家伙在水里呆了大概 10 个小时，但水温却高达 76 度，”诺顿说。 “这是不同的一年，他不可能成功。”
海岸警卫队仍在调查船员从游轮坠落的情况。皇家加勒比集团承认了这一事件，并表示正在协助这名员工。
公司发言人在给哥伦比亚广播公司的一份声明中表示：“在这个困难时期，我们正在向我们的机组人员提供支持和帮助。为了尊重我们员工的隐私，我们没有更多的细节可以分享。”

title_en: GOP Rep. Hill says he'll weigh whether Hegseth's actions merit impeachment
title_zh: 共和党众议员希尔表示，他将权衡赫格斯的行为是否值得弹劾
summary: GOP Rep. French Hill of Arkansas was noncommittal about whether he would support an impeachment push against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
summary_zh: 阿肯色州共和党众议员弗伦奇·希尔 (French Hill) 对于是否支持弹劾国防部长皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth) 不置可否。
body_en: GOP Rep. French Hill says he'll weigh whether Hegseth's actions merit "impeachment versus some other disciplinary action" - CBS News

Washington — GOP Rep. French Hill of Arkansas was noncommittal on Sunday about whether he would support an impeachment push against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth as lawmakers are poised to return to Capitol Hill this week for the first time since voters delivered widespread rebuke in the midterm elections of the GOP — and the war in Iran.

"I want to hear the debate on it to see if it merits impeachment versus some other disciplinary action or action by the president if he's not getting the job done in leading the Department of War," Hill said on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan ."

Hegseth is expected to be under the microscope this week as long-brewing anger has come to the fore following the midterm elections , where Republicans saw brutal losses as many voters cited concerns about the war in Iran and its impact on the cost of living. Before lawmakers left town for the campaign trail, outgoing GOP Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky introduced articles of impeachment against Hegseth. This week, Massie said he plans to push ahead with forcing the vote.

Hill acknowledged that he's not satisfied with how the war has been handled. And he added that, "The commander in chief has to take the responsibility for the strategy of conducting the war and how it's been conducted."
"But I'll tell you one thing: There's nobody in America that wants Iran to have a nuclear weapon," Hill said. "This has been a goal of the United States for five decades."
Asked whether Hegseth should be impeached, Hill said, "The question is for the president: Should he continue to serve as the Secretary of War."
Hill also drew a distinction between Hegseth's job performance and whether he's committed impeachable offenses. Under the Constitution, the basis for impeachment is "high Crimes and Misdemeanors."
"If you don't think he's done a good job conducting his job, that doesn't mean per se that he's committed an impeachable offense," Hill said.
The Arkansas Republican said that if Hegseth isn't "conducting his mission in the right way," then "then the president ought to make a change there."
"The question is: Are we leading at the Pentagon in the right way or not the right way?" Hill said. "That's very separate from whether or not somebody's committed an impeachable offense."

body_zh: 共和党众议员弗伦奇·希尔表示，他将权衡赫格斯的行为是否值得“弹劾或其他纪律处分” - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
华盛顿——周日，来自阿肯色州的共和党众议员弗伦奇·希尔 (French Hill) 对于是否支持弹劾国防部长皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth) 不置可否，因为自选民对共和党中期选举和伊朗战争进行广泛谴责以来，议员们准备于本周首次返回国会山。
希尔在“与玛格丽特·布伦南一起面对国家”节目中说：“我想听听对此的辩论，看看如果总统没有完成领导战争部的工作，是否值得弹劾或采取其他纪律处分或总统行动。”
预计赫格斯本周将受到密切关注，因为中期选举后酝酿已久的愤怒情绪凸显出来，共和党人在中期选举中遭受惨重损失，因为许多选民对伊朗战争及其对生活成本的影响表示担忧。在议员们离开小镇参加竞选活动之前，即将离任的肯塔基州共和党众议员托马斯·马西提出了针对赫格斯的弹劾条款。本周，马西表示，他计划推动强制投票。
希尔承认他对战争的处理方式并不满意。他补充说，“总司令必须对进行战争的战略以及如何进行战争承担责任。”
“但我要告诉你一件事：美国没有人希望伊朗拥有核武器，”希尔说。 “这是美国五十年来的目标。”
当被问及是否应该弹劾赫格斯时，希尔说，“问题是针对总统的：他是否应该继续担任战争部长。”
希尔还对赫格斯的工作表现和他是否犯有可弹劾的罪行进行了区分。根据宪法，弹劾的依据是“重罪和轻罪”。
希尔说：“如果你认为他的工作表现不佳，这并不意味着他犯下了可弹劾的罪行。”
这位阿肯色州共和党人表示，如果赫格斯没有“以正确的方式履行他的使命”，那么“那么总统应该做出改变。”
“问题是：我们在五角大楼的领导方式正确还是错误？”希尔说。 “这与某人是否犯有可弹劾的罪行截然不同。”

title_en: Small plane crashes into pickup truck on busy Florida highway
title_zh: 小型飞机在繁忙的佛罗里达高速公路上撞上皮卡车
summary: No one was injured after emergency landing in Fort Myers 50 minutes after takeoff with two people onboard A small plane crashed into the rear of a pickup truck as it made an emergency landing on a busy Florida highway on Saturday but miraculously no one was in
summary_zh: 一架小型飞机起飞50分钟后紧急降落在迈尔斯堡，机上有两人，无人受伤
body_en: No one was injured after emergency landing in Fort Myers 50 minutes after takeoff with two people onboard
A small plane crashed into the rear of a pickup truck as it made an emergency landing on a busy Florida highway on Saturday but miraculously no one was injured in the dramatic incident.
Video footage obtained from the sheriff’s office shows a Cessna 172 grazing over the truck as it approached the ground for a complete landing on a road in Fort Meyers at about 11.45am on Saturday.
The aircraft made an emergency landing after the pilot reported an engine issue, according to a Federal Aviation Agency (FAA) statement .
All nine people onboard business jet that crashed in Florida have died
The plane took off from Sebring, Florida, around 11am on Saturday before it made the emergency landing about 50 minutes later, according to flight tracking data .
There were two people on board the aircraft and the pickup truck was traveling eastbound on Bayshore Road.
There were no reported injuries on the scene, according the Lee county sheriff’s office.
“Couldn’t have been a better outcome. Grateful doesn’t come close!” Carmine Marceno, Lee county’s sheriff, shared in a post to X .
LCSO Patrol & Florida’s department of transportation safely relocated the aircraft while the FAA is working to assume the investigation, Marceno added.
The FAA is the lead agency on the investigation into the incident.
The emergency landing comes one week after a business jet carrying nine people nose-dived into a south Florida neighborhood and erupted into a giant fireball.
body_zh: 起飞50分钟后紧急降落在迈尔斯堡，机上有两人，无人受伤
周六，一架小型飞机在佛罗里达州一条繁忙的高速公路上紧急降落时撞上了一辆皮卡车的后部，但奇迹般地没有人在这场戏剧性的事件中受伤。
从警长办公室获得的视频片段显示，周六上午 11 点 45 分左右，一架塞斯纳 172 飞机在卡车接近地面准备完全降落在迈耶斯堡的道路上时掠过卡车。
根据美国联邦航空局（FAA）的声明，在飞行员报告发动机出现问题后，飞机紧急着陆。
佛罗里达州坠毁的公务机上九人全部遇难
根据航班跟踪数据，这架飞机于周六上午 11 点左右从佛罗里达州赛百灵起飞，约 50 分钟后紧急降落。
飞机上有两人，皮卡车当时正在湾岸路向东行驶。
据李县治安官办公室称，现场没有人员受伤的报告。
“这是一个再好不过的结果了。感激之情根本无法接近！”李县治安官 Carmine Marceno 在 X 上分享了一篇帖子。
马塞诺补充说，LCSO 巡逻队和佛罗里达州交通部安全地转移了这架飞机，而美国联邦航空局正在着手调查。
美国联邦航空局是调查该事件的牵头机构。
一周前，一架载有九名乘客的商务飞机急速降落在佛罗里达州南部的一个社区，并爆发出一个巨大的火球。

title_en: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries says he is a ‘hard yes’ on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
title_zh: 众议院少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯表示，他对弹劾国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯表示“坚决同意”
summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said he is a “hard yes” on supporting impeachment efforts against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
summary_zh: 纽约州众议院少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯表示，他“坚决支持”弹劾国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯
body_en: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said he is a “hard yes” on supporting impeachment efforts against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, which are expected to be brought to a vote this week.
Asked in an interview on ABC’s “This Week” whether he would support Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., in his efforts to impeach Hegseth, Jeffries confirmed he supported the push.

“I’m a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution,” Jeffries said. “The so-called secretary of defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe.”

Jeffries’ support marks a major endorsement of impeachment efforts against Hegseth and signals how other House Democrats could ultimately vote on the measure. The impeachment push also tests how far lawmakers are willing to go to oust the top Pentagon official after voters have given low marks to the administration’s handling of the war in Iran, which factored into midterms.

Asked on ABC whether Jeffries believed all other House Democrats would support the impeachment resolution, he said that they would “have that conversation Tuesday morning.” The House is back in session this week, and the impeachment resolution is expected to be filed early this week with a vote to follow.

Massie has been a vocal critic of Hegseth and the war in Iran. He previously filed a resolution to impeach Hegseth in September, but Republican leaders canceled planned votes and the House left early, pushing the vote to after the election.

NBC News reported last week that President Donald Trump has told allies that he was considering replacing Hegseth. Trump, though, has publicly denied that he is planning to replace the secretary, telling reporters last week that Hegseth was “doing a very good job.”
At the same time, Hegseth has forcefully pushed back on Massie’s impeachment plans, referring to the congressman in a social media video last week as a “disgruntled, defeated congressman.”
“It’s all about the politics of personal destruction,” Hegseth said in the video. “Didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me. You can rest assured of that.”

Massie, though, said in a social media post last week that his “Hegseth impeachment resolution is a much gentler version of what’s coming when Dem’s control Congress.” Democrats, Massie said, would “have hearings & trials.”
This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.
Megan Brand is a politics reporter for NBC News.
body_zh: 纽约州众议院少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯表示，他“坚决支持”对国防部长皮特·赫格斯的弹劾努力，弹劾预计将于本周进行投票。
在接受美国广播公司“本周”采访时被问及是否会支持肯塔基州共和党众议员托马斯·马西弹劾赫格斯的努力时，杰弗里斯证实他支持这一努力。
“我对赫格塞斯决议坚决支持，”杰弗里斯说。 “所谓的国防部长滥用权力，破坏了我们的国家安全，并在伊朗策划了这场鲁莽且代价高昂的选择战争，这使美国人民的物价飞涨，使国家变得不那么安全。”
杰弗里斯的支持标志着对赫格赛斯弹劾努力的重大支持，并表明其他众议院民主党人最终将如何对该措施进行投票。弹劾行动还考验了议员们愿意在多大程度上罢免五角大楼高级官员，因为选民对政府处理伊朗战争的方式给予了低分，而伊朗战争是中期选举的一个因素。
当被问及杰弗里斯是否相信所有其他众议院民主党人都会支持弹劾决议时，他表示他们将“在周二早上进行对话”。众议院本周重新开会，弹劾决议预计将于本周初提交，随后进行投票。
马西一直直言不讳地批评赫格斯和伊朗战争。他此前于9月提交了弹劾赫格塞斯的决议，但共和党领导人取消了原计划的投票，众议院提前离开，将投票推迟到大选后。
NBC 新闻上周报道称，唐纳德·特朗普总统已告诉盟友，他正在考虑取代赫格塞斯。不过，特朗普公开否认他计划更换国务卿，并上周告诉记者，赫格塞斯“做得非常好”。
与此同时，赫格斯强力反击了马西的弹劾计划，他在上周的社交媒体视频中称这位国会议员为“心怀不满、失败的国会议员”。
“这都是关于个人毁灭的政治，”赫格斯在视频中说。 “这对特朗普总统不起作用，对我也不起作用。这一点你可以放心。”
不过，马西上周在社交媒体帖子中表示，他的“赫格斯弹劾决议是民主党控制国会时的温和版本。”马西说，民主党将“举行听证会和审判”。
这是一个发展的故事。请回来查看更新。
梅根·布兰德是 NBC 新闻的政治记者。

title_en: Scoop: Trump asked Netanyahu to move on Gaza peace plan in post-election call
title_zh: 独家新闻：特朗普在大选后电话会议中要求内塔尼亚胡推进加沙和平计划
summary: President Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a phone call Thursday that he wants him to take steps to implement his Gaza peace plan , according to two sources with knowledge of the matter. Why it matters: The roadmap calls for disarmin
summary_zh: 特朗普总统周四在电话中告诉以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡，他希望他采取措施实施他的加沙和平协议
body_en: President Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a phone call Thursday that he wants him to take steps to implement his Gaza peace plan , according to two sources with knowledge of the matter.

Why it matters: The roadmap calls for disarming Hamas and demilitarizing Gaza, as well as transferring responsibility for governing the enclave to a new Palestinian technocratic government. But it has been on hold for months because of the Israeli elections held on Oct. 27.
The Trump administration did not want implementation of the plan to become a politically explosive issue during the Israeli election campaign.

Trump endorsed Netanyahu shortly before the election. Now that it's over, the president wants to forge ahead with his Gaza plan, regardless of whether Netanyahu or his opposition forms a new government.

Catch up quick: A year ago, Israel and Hamas agreed to the first phase of Trump's 20-point plan, which led to a ceasefire in the Gaza war and the release of the last 20 living hostages taken during the Oct. 7, 2023 attacks.

Trump's Board of Peace, which was established as part of the Gaza agreement, has been working for months on an implementation plan that includes the establishment of a Palestinian technocratic government and an International Stabilization Force.

Last July, the Board of Peace reached an agreement with Hamas on a 15-point plan to disarm the armed groups in Gaza and transfer civilian and security control to the new Palestinian technocratic government.
Since then, Netanyahu's government has largely refused to move forward with implementing it, mostly for domestic political reasons.

In an August visit to Israel, Trump adviser and son-in-law Jared Kushner told Netanyahu that Hamas for the first time had agreed to disarm. He urged the Israeli prime minister to take steps to test whether that commitment was real.
Netanyahu was and still is extremely skeptical that Hamas will ever demilitarize. He says the group is reconstituting and rearming in Gaza.

Zoom in: Over the past three months, Trump's Board of Peace has been working with the Israeli government and military to refine details of the plan and address Israeli concerns about demilitarization in Gaza.
A U.S. official said the process would be gradual. Reconstruction would only begin after progress in disarming Hamas had been verified.
Trump's Board of Peace unveiled a six-month, $2.45 billion initial recovery plan for Gaza during the U.N. General Assembly in September.
The 66-project proposal offers one of the most comprehensive roadmaps yet for what the early months of post-war recovery and governance in Gaza would look like.
But for the plan to move forward, the Board of Peace needs Israel and Hamas to cooperate.
A source with knowledge of the details said the Trump administration, Board of Peace and Israel agree that the plan remains the best way forward and that there is no credible alternative.
Behind the scenes: Secretary of State Marco Rubio as well as Kushner and Trump envoy Steve Witkoff also participated in the call between the president and Netanyahu.
A source with knowledge of the details described the call, which Netanyahu initiated, as constructive. It also addressed the war in Iran.
The White House and the Israeli prime minister's office did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
State of play: A day after the call, former British Prime Minister Tony Blair, who is a member of the Board of Peace, visited Israel.
body_zh: 据两位知情人士透露，特朗普总统在周四的电话中告诉以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡，他希望他采取措施实施他的加沙和平计划。
重要性：该路线图呼吁解除哈马斯武装，使加沙非军事化，并将管理该飞地的责任移交给新的巴勒斯坦技术官僚政府。但由于 10 月 27 日举行的以色列选举，该计划已被搁置数月。
特朗普政府不希望该计划的实施成为以色列竞选期间的政治爆炸性问题。
特朗普在大选前不久支持内塔尼亚胡。现在一切都结束了，总统希望继续推进他的加沙计划，无论内塔尼亚胡还是他的反对派是否组建新政府。
快速赶上：一年前，以色列和哈马斯同意特朗普 20 点计划的第一阶段，这导致加沙战争停火，并释放了 2023 年 10 月 7 日袭击中被劫持的最后 20 名人质。
作为加沙协议一部分而成立的特朗普和平委员会几个月来一直在制定一项实施计划，其中包括建立巴勒斯坦技术官僚政府和国际稳定部队。
去年7月，和平委员会与哈马斯就一项15点计划达成协议，解除加沙武装团体的武装，并将民事和安全控制权移交给新的巴勒斯坦技术官僚政府。
从那时起，内塔尼亚胡政府基本上拒绝推进该计划的实施，主要是出于国内政治原因。
在八月访问以色列时，特朗普顾问兼女婿贾里德·库什纳告诉内塔尼亚胡，哈马斯首次同意解除武装。他敦促以色列总理采取措施检验这一承诺是否真实。
内塔尼亚胡曾经并且仍然对哈马斯是否会非军事化持极其怀疑的态度。他说，该组织正在加沙重组并重新武装。
放大：在过去的三个月里，特朗普的和平委员会一直在与以色列政府和军方合作，完善该计划的细节，并解决以色列对加沙非军事化的担忧。
一位美国官员表示，这一过程将是渐进的。只有在哈马斯解除武装的进展得到证实之后，重建工作才会开始。
特朗普的和平委员会在 9 月份的联合国大会期间公布了一项为期六个月、耗资 24.5 亿美元的加沙初步恢复计划。
这份包含 66 个项目的提案为加沙战后最初几个月的恢复和治理提供了迄今为止最全面的路线图之一。
但为了推进该计划，和平委员会需要以色列和哈马斯的合作。
一位了解细节的消息人士称，特朗普政府、和平委员会和以色列一致认为，该计划仍然是前进的最佳途径，并且没有可靠的替代方案。
幕后：国务卿马可·卢比奥以及库什纳和特朗普特使史蒂夫·威特科夫也参加了总统与内塔尼亚胡之间的通话。
一位了解细节的消息人士称，内塔尼亚胡发起的这次通话具有建设性。它还谈到了伊朗战争。
白宫和以色列总理办公室没有立即回应置评请求。
事态发展：通话后的第二天，和平委员会成员、英国前首相托尼·布莱尔访问了以色列。

title_en: Texas's 'Blue Tsunami' has former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke 'over the moon'
title_zh: 德克萨斯州的“蓝色海啸”让前德克萨斯州国会议员贝托·奥罗克“欣喜若狂”
summary: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke about how past efforts by him and other Democrats helped the party win big in Texas in the midterms.
summary_zh: NPR 的罗布·施密茨 (Rob Schmitz) 与前德克萨斯州国会议员贝托·奥罗克 (Beto O'Rourke) 谈论他和其他民主党人过去的努力如何帮助该党在德克萨斯州大获全胜
body_en: Texas's 'Blue Tsunami' has former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke 'over the moon' NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke about how past efforts by him and other Democrats helped the party win big in Texas in the midterms.
NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke about how past efforts by him and other Democrats helped the party win big in Texas in the midterms.

While Texas' populist roots may have laid the foundation for Democratic victories in the state, they weren't the only factor that helped Texas Democrats win on Tuesday. Former Texas congressman and presidential candidate Beto O'Rourke has helped pave the way for Democrat victories in the Lone Star State. You might remember his 2018 bid to unseat longstanding Republican Senator Ted Cruz. Ultimately, he lost by just a few percentage points. In 2022, he ran against Governor Greg Abbott and again lost, that time by only a slightly larger margin. Beto O'Rourke joins us now. Welcome.

SCHMITZ: So I feel like you have been out of the national spotlight for a while, but perhaps that's because you've been hard at work on the ground there in Texas mobilizing voters. Tell us about that.

O'ROURKE: After the Senate race, we asked ourselves, what would it take to win in Texas? And from that, we started a group called Powered By People, and it's thousands of folks - many of whom volunteered on that Senate race - who get trained as volunteer deputy registrars, meet young people in person, get them registered and then, importantly, stay in touch with them and help them overcome the obstacles in a state that makes it harder than any other in the nation for young people to register and to vote, to help them participate in our politics.
SCHMITZ: Young folks showed up big time for Democrats this cycle. An NBC exit poll shows that 79% of voters under the age of 30 voted for Talarico. What do you think appealed to that demographic?

O'ROURKE: I think, first and foremost, James Talarico, who described this contest as not between a Democrat and a Republican or right versus left, but top versus bottom. When I spend time on these college campuses or at (inaudible) or clubs with young people as we help them to get registered and I ask them what's important to them, they are absolutely disgusted with the concentration of wealth and privilege and power in this country. They ask me about the Epstein files and say, you know, how can the wealthiest, most powerful men rape and traffic girls and women with complete impunity? How is it that we're at war again in the Middle East? Why are we complicit in this genocide in Gaza? Why is no one doing anything about these things?

And then at home in Texas, the minimum wage is 7.25. It's the hardest state in the nation in which to see a doctor, and schoolteachers are working two or three jobs to make ends meet. These aren't Republican or Democrat issues. They're issues of basic justice, and I think that young people have the most acute sense of what is right or wrong. They are impatient with excuses or equivocation or blaming it on one party or another. They want solutions, and they want people to deliver.

SCHMITZ: That's interesting. I mean, this is something that we spoke with our previous guest, David Griscom - he's an author in Texas - about, that economic populism was one of the reasons that James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa won both the Senate and gubernatorial election. Is there anything that Democrats can learn from how this played out and what really matters to Texans?

O'ROURKE: I think the takeaway is it is incredibly important for Democrats now in power to deliver for the people they represent in ways that they can feel immediately. So raising the minimum wage - if you're working for $7.25 an hour, you're probably working two or three of those jobs to make ends meet. Raising that minimum wage will be felt immediately.

You know, if you can't afford to see a doctor right now, and you're suffering as a result of that, being able to, through Medicaid expansion, see a provider - that's going to change your life immediately. And the follow-on effects of being able to afford tuition or down payment on a home or an automobile, these are significant material differences in people's lives.

And so we have high expectations for Gina and James. And really, as you probably know, every single statewide office was won by a Democrat. The Democrats also picked a majority in the state House. They now have the opportunity to deliver for people. And so while we're excited and we're celebrating their victories, we're also understanding there's accountability, responsibility, and the clock is ticking.

SCHMITZ: You obviously had a lot to do with this popularity of Democrats that we are seeing right now. I mean, you, of course, ran for Senate. You ran for governor. You lost time and time again for both of those races. But a lot in the background was gained. How is this feeling for you right now, seeing these wins?

O'ROURKE: I'm over the moon. I mean, you know, my wife, Amy, and I, in 2016, when Trump won - I happened to be in Congress at the time - we looked at each other and we said, we have got to do something more. What we've been doing so far serving in Congress is insufficient to the task at hand, this threat of authoritarianism and fascism and the rise of this oligarchy in America. We needed to do something.

And from that was born this crazy snowball's-chance-in-Texas idea of running for Senate in a state that last elected a Democrat to the Senate in 1988. And I was joined by hundreds of thousands - and by the end, millions - of my fellow Texans who believed in that dream. And so it wasn't so much, you know, should Beto O'Rourke serve in the Senate or, you know, my name on an office or on the ballot. It is, can we change this state? And by extension, given the outsized importance of Texas, can we change this country?
SCHMITZ: Well, Beto O'Rourke, since I've got you here, I should ask you whether you have plans to run for president in 2028.

O'ROURKE: No, I don't, but I am going to be involved one way or another. This extraordinary experiment 250 years in the making that is the product of so much service and sacrifice and struggle - all of us must do all that we can to keep it going. So that's my mission. That's what I'm going to be focused on. And wherever I can be useful or helpful, that's where you'll find me.
body_zh: 德克萨斯州的“蓝色海啸”让前德克萨斯州国会议员贝托·奥罗克欣喜若狂 NPR 的罗布·施密茨与前德克萨斯州国会议员贝托·奥罗克谈论了他和其他民主党人过去的努力如何帮助该党在中期选举中在德克萨斯州大获全胜。
NPR 的罗布·施密茨 (Rob Schmitz) 与前德克萨斯州国会议员贝托·奥罗克 (Beto O'Rourke) 谈论了他和其他民主党人过去的努力如何帮助该党在德克萨斯州中期选举中大获全胜。

虽然德克萨斯州的民粹主义根源可能为民主党在该州的胜利奠定了基础，但这并不是帮助德克萨斯州民主党周二获胜的唯一因素。前德克萨斯州国会议员和总统候选人贝托·奥罗克帮助为民主党在孤星州的胜利铺平了道路。您可能还记得他在 2018 年试图推翻长期担任共和党参议员的特德·克鲁兹 (Ted Cruz)。最终，他只输了几个百分点。 2022 年，他与州长格雷格·阿博特 (Greg Abbott) 竞选，再次落败，只是以稍大的优势落败。贝托·奥罗克现在加入我们。欢迎。
施密茨：所以我觉得你已经离开全国聚光灯一段时间了，但这也许是因为你一直在德克萨斯州努力动员选民。告诉我们这一点。
奥罗克：参议院竞选结束后，我们问自己，怎样才能在德克萨斯州获胜？从那时起，我们成立了一个名为“Powered By People”的团体，有成千上万的人——其中许多人自愿参加了参议院竞选——接受了志愿副登记员的培训，亲自与年轻人会面，让他们登记，然后，重要的是，与他们保持联系，帮助他们克服在这个州比全国任何其他年轻人都更难登记和投票的障碍，帮助他们参与我们的政治。
施密茨：这个周期年轻人在民主党中表现出色。 NBC 的出口民意调查显示，79% 30 岁以下的选民投票支持塔拉里科。您认为什么对这一人群有吸引力？

奥罗克：我认为，首先也是最重要的是詹姆斯·塔拉里科（James Talarico），他将这场比赛描述为不是民主党和共和党之间的竞争，也不是右翼与左翼之间的竞争，而是上层与下层之间的竞争。当我花时间在这些大学校园或（听不清）或俱乐部与年轻人一起帮助他们注册时，我问他们什么对他们来说是重要的，他们对这个国家的财富、特权和权力的集中感到绝对厌恶。他们问我关于爱泼斯坦的档案，并说，你知道，最富有、最有权势的男人怎么能强奸和贩卖女孩和妇女而完全不受惩罚？我们中东怎么又开战了？为什么我们是加沙种族灭绝的同谋？为什么没有人对这些事情采取任何行动？
然后在德克萨斯州，最低工资是7.25。这是全国看病最困难的州，学校老师要打两三份工才能维持生计。这些不是共和党或民主党的问题。它们是基本正义的问题，我认为年轻人对是非的判断力最敏锐。他们对借口、模棱两可或将责任归咎于一方或另一方不耐烦。他们想要解决方案，并且希望人们能够提供解决方案。
施密茨：这很有趣。我的意思是，这就是我们与我们的上一位嘉宾戴维·格里斯科姆（David Griscom）（他是德克萨斯州的一位作家）谈到的，经济民粹主义是詹姆斯·塔拉里科（James Talarico）和吉娜·伊诺霍萨（Gina Hinojosa）赢得参议院和州长选举的原因之一。民主党人可以从事情的发展过程中学到什么以及对德克萨斯人真正重要的事情吗？
奥罗克：我认为，对于现在掌权的民主党人来说，以他们能够立即感受到的方式为他们所代表的人民提供服务是非常重要的。因此，提高最低工资——如果你的工作时薪为 7.25 美元，你可能会做其中的两到三份工作来维持收支平衡。提高最低工资将立即得到体现。
您知道，如果您现在看不起医生，并且因此而遭受痛苦，那么通过医疗补助扩展，您可以去看医生，这将立即改变您的生活。能够负担学费或房屋或汽车首付的后续影响，这些都是人们生活中的重大物质差异。
所以我们对吉娜和詹姆斯抱有很高的期望。事实上，正如你可能知道的那样，每一个全州的职位都是由民主党赢得的。民主党还赢得了州议会的多数席位。他们现在有机会为人们服务。因此，当我们兴奋并庆祝他们的胜利时，我们也理解其中的责任和责任，而且时间在流逝。
施密茨：我们现在看到的民主党受欢迎程度显然与你有很大关系。我的意思是，你当然竞选参议员。你竞选州长。在这两场比赛中你一次又一次地失败。但在后台却收获颇多。看到这些胜利，你现在感觉如何？
奥罗克：我欣喜若狂。我的意思是，你知道，我和我的妻子艾米，在 2016 年特朗普获胜时——我当时恰好在国会——我们互相看着对方，我们说，我们必须做更多的事情。到目前为止，我们在国会所做的工作不足以完成手头的任务，即威权主义和法西斯主义的威胁以及美国寡头政治的崛起。我们需要做点什么。
于是，这个疯狂的德克萨斯州滚雪球般的想法诞生了，即在 1988 年最后一次选举民主党人进入参议院的州竞选参议员。数十万——最后是数百万——相信这个梦想的德克萨斯同胞加入了我的行列。因此，你知道，贝托·奥罗克是否应该在参议院任职，或者你知道，我的名字出现在办公室或选票上，这并不是那么重要。是的，我们能改变这种状态吗？推而广之，鉴于德克萨斯州的巨大重要性，我们可以改变这个国家吗？
施密茨：贝托·奥罗克，既然你来了，我应该问你是否有计划在 2028 年竞选总统。
奥罗克：不，我不这样做，但我会以某种方式参与其中。这项非凡的实验历时 250 年，是大量服务、牺牲和奋斗的成果 - 我们所有人都必须竭尽全力让它继续下去。这就是我的使命。这就是我要关注的重点。只要我能提供帮助，您就可以找到我。

summary_zh: 密歇根当选参议员的前同僚回忆起他在英国读大学的时光，以及他对加冕鸡肉三明治的热爱。
body_en: Abdul El-Sayed’s Oxford years: PhD, political influences and sporting distinction | Abdul El-Sayed
Michigan senator-elect’s former peers recall his time at university in Britain – and his love of coronation chicken sandwiches
In the cold, twilight days of 2008, inside the University of Michigan’s fortress-like Fleming administration building, one student was given a particularly adulatory sendoff.

Mary Sue Coleman, president of the university at the time, convened a ceremony for the latest Rhodes scholar heading to the University of Oxford: Abdul El-Sayed. “There is no doubt among anyone who crosses his path that he will achieve all he sets out to accomplish and more,” she declared to a room full of the university’s leaders, calling the medical PhD student the “epitome of the engaged intellect”.
She even recalled Bill Clinton’s response to a speech made by El-Sayed in 2007, with the former US president remarking: “I wish every person in the world could have heard you speak today.”

For those who ran into El-Sayed months later in autumn 2009 when he finally crossed the pond, these words of praise rang true. “He always seemed very driven,” says Elias Rothblatt, who played lacrosse alongside Michigan’s senator-elect more than 15 years ago. El-Sayed was captain of Oxford’s lacrosse team and student journalists at the time described him as a “defensive master” in the sport .

Rothblatt, 36, who works in fintech, says El-Sayed was a “very fierce competitor” on the field and a “wonderful” captain. “He had a great sense of humour. He struck a really good mix of being friends with other people on the team but also setting the tone and helping lead the team and keep things, keeping serious.”

Off the field, Rothblatt says, El-Sayed was equally “fun and friendly”. He says: “It was always a pleasure to run into him. He was with his wife sometimes and she was wonderful too.” El-Sayed also had a fixation on a resolutely British sandwich: coronation chicken. Speaking to the Times, Ricardo Chasebi, owner of a now-closed cafe in Oxford’s covered market, recalled El-Sayed’s order as a grilled ciabatta filled with coronation chicken, cheddar, peppers and red onion that was topped with lettuce and tomato.

He eventually placed El-Sayed’s version on the menu, naming it “the Abdul”. The senator-to-be was so keen on Chasebi’s sandwiches that he would call ahead from the airport and say: “I’ll be in Oxford in two hours, don’t shut until I get there.” El-Sayed even handed Chasebi a copy of his doctoral thesis, where he thanked the cafe owner in the acknowledgments for “nourishing my stomach and my soul”.
Rothblatt has tried the Abdul sandwich. “It’s good,” he says. El-Sayed also had a penchant for Nando’s, organising meetings there with his fellow Rhodes scholar cohort.

While he eventually settled into Oxford life, things didn’t start smoothly for El-Sayed. He did not enjoy his course at first and flew back to Michigan two weeks before his first term ended. And based on a recent outburst, where he told a Sky News reporter: “You know how many votes I want to get in the UK? Zero,” you might assume he was, at best, apathetic about his time in Britain. But that is not the case. In his memoir, Healing Politics: A Doctor’s Journey into the Heart of Our Political Epidemic, El-Sayed wrote: “My classmates in Oxford taught me more than I could learn in any classroom.” And in several articles El-Sayed wrote for the Guardian, he expressed an appreciation for Britain and, in particular, its political system.

In one piece, where he declared that UK democracy had the “upper hand” on the US, El-Sayed expressed his awe at a parliamentary hustings in Tower Hamlets, east London before the 2010 general election where all of the candidates were of Bengali heritage, reflecting the demographics of the local area. He opined: “As an Arab-American, the likelihood of ever having the opportunity to vote for an Arab-American candidate for national office during my lifetime is minimal.”

But this week, he did have the opportunity to do so, being able to cast the ballot for himself. He was joined by more than 2.5 million others who followed suit and elected El-Sayed as the country’s first Muslim senator.

Rothblatt is “very excited” to see what El-Sayed will do in the Senate. “I think he’s going to do a fantastic job. Back then, he was a talented, ambitious person who had some really good ideas about what he wanted to do in the world. Now he’s continuing to bring those to life,” he says.

body_zh: 阿卜杜勒·赛义德的牛津岁月：博士、政治影响和体育成就 |阿卜杜勒·赛义德
密歇根当选参议员的前同僚回忆起他在英国读大学的时光，以及他对加冕鸡肉三明治的热爱
2008 年寒冷的黄昏，在密歇根大学堡垒般的弗莱明行政大楼内，一名学生受到了特别热烈的欢送。
时任牛津大学校长玛丽·苏·科尔曼 (Mary Sue Coleman) 为最新一位前往牛津大学的罗德学者阿卜杜勒·埃尔·赛义德 (Abdul El-Sayed) 举行了仪式。 “毫无疑问，任何遇到他的人都会实现他设定的目标，甚至更多，”她向满屋子的大学领导宣称，并称这位医学博士生是“智慧的缩影”。
她甚至回忆起比尔·克林顿 (Bill Clinton) 对 2007 年埃尔·赛义德 (El-Sayed) 演讲的回应，这位美国前总统说道：“我希望世界上每个人今天都能听到你的演讲。”
对于那些几个月后、即 2009 年秋天，当埃尔赛义德终于渡过大西洋时遇见他的人来说，这些赞美之词听起来是真实的。 “他看起来总是很有干劲，”埃利亚斯·罗斯布拉特 (Elias Rothblatt) 说道，15 多年前，他曾与密歇根州当选参议员一起打长曲棍球。埃尔-赛义德是牛津长曲棍球队的队长，当时的学生记者称他为这项运动的“防守大师”。
36 岁的罗斯布拉特在金融科技领域工作，他表示埃尔-赛义德是球场上“非常激烈的竞争者”，也是一位“出色的”队长。 “他很有幽默感。他与团队中的其他人成为朋友，同时也定下了基调，帮助领导团队，让事情保持严肃。”
罗斯布拉特说，在场外，埃尔-赛义德同样“有趣且友好”。他说：“见到他总是很高兴。他有时和他的妻子在一起，她也很棒。”埃尔-赛义德还痴迷于一种绝对的英式三明治：加冕鸡。牛津室内市场一家现已关闭的咖啡馆老板里卡多·查塞比 (Ricardo Chasebi) 在接受《泰晤士报》采访时回忆，埃尔·赛义德点的菜是一份烤夏巴塔面包，里面填满加冕鸡、切达干酪、辣椒和红洋葱，上面撒上生菜和番茄。
他最终将埃尔赛义德的版本放在菜单上，并将其命名为“阿卜杜勒”。这位准参议员非常喜欢 Chasebi 的三明治，以至于他会提前从机场打电话说：“我将在两小时内到达牛津，在我到达之前不要关门。”埃尔-赛义德甚至递给查塞比一份他的博士论文副本，他在致谢词中感谢咖啡馆老板“滋养了我的胃和灵魂”。
罗斯布拉特尝试过阿卜杜勒三明治。 “这很好，”他说。埃尔-赛义德也对 Nando's 情有独钟，他在那里组织了与他的罗德学者同伴的会议。

虽然埃尔赛义德最终适应了牛津的生活，但一切的开始并不顺利。他一开始并不喜欢他的课程，并在第一个学期结束前两周飞回密歇根。根据他最近的一次爆发，​​他对天空新闻记者说：“你知道我想在英国获得多少选票吗？零。”你可能会认为他充其量只是对自己在英国的时光漠不关心。但事实并非如此。埃尔赛义德在他的回忆录《治愈政治：一位医生深入政治流行病核心的旅程》中写道：“我在牛津的同学教给我的东西比我在任何课堂上学到的都多。”埃尔-赛义德在为《卫报》撰写的几篇文章中表达了对英国，特别是其政治制度的赞赏。
在一篇文章中，埃尔-赛义德宣称英国民主对美国“占上风”，他对 2010 年大选前伦敦东部塔尔哈姆莱茨举行的议会竞选表示敬畏，当时所有候选人都是孟加拉裔，反映了当地的人口结构。他认为：“作为一名阿拉伯裔美国人，在我有生之年有机会投票给阿拉伯裔美国国家公职候选人的可能性微乎其微。”
但本周，他确实有机会这样做，能够为自己投票。超过 250 万其他人也纷纷效仿，选举埃尔赛义德为该国第一位穆斯林参议员。
罗斯布拉特“非常兴奋”看到埃尔赛义德将在参议院做什么。 “我认为他会做得非常出色。当时，他是一个才华横溢、雄心勃勃的人，对于自己想在这个世界上做什么有一些非常好的想法。现在他正在继续将这些想法变为现实，”他说。

title_en: How Hinojosa’s win in Texas could bite Beshear
title_zh: 伊诺霍萨在德克萨斯州的胜利会给贝希尔带来怎样的影响
summary: Latino operatives for months pressured Andy Beshear and the Democratic Governors Association to back Gina Hinojosa. Now her win is blowing back on them.
summary_zh: 几个月来，拉丁裔特工向安迪·贝希尔和民主党州长协会施压，要求他们支持吉娜·伊诺霍萨。现在她的胜利正在回击
body_en: AUSTIN, Texas — Gina Hinojosa’s stunning victory put Texas at the epicenter of a political earthquake — and the aftershocks could upend Andy Beshear’s path to the White House.

For months, increasingly frustrated Hinojosa allies publicly and privately pressured the Democratic Governors Association, which Beshear chairs, to help push her over the finish line, as many national Democrats and donors stayed on the sidelines. On Tuesday, Hinojosa dominated the race for the Texas governor’s mansion, riding a blue wave that swept Democrats into power across the country, including flipping six governorships in states won by President Donald Trump.
Latino operatives who spoke with POLITICO feel vindicated — and are turning their knives on Beshear ahead of a potential 2028 presidential bid.
“His presidential campaign is over,” said Sergio Gonzalez, a Democratic operative working on programs to turn out Latino voters in the midterms.

Beshear “doesn't understand politics in the way that a president needs to understand politics,” and “failed Latino voters and Texas voters and Democrats in this moment,” said Gonzalez, who previously worked as a top aide to former Vice President Kamala Harris’ campaign.

Hinojosa’s race became the ultimate underdog campaign — a push to conquer a state Democrats had all but abandoned, with a candidate from the increasingly conservative Rio Grande Valley who her team was betting could turn out Latino voters in droves. Many national Democrats privately believed Hinojosa didn’t have a shot. But as public polling showed her closing the gap with three-term incumbent GOP Gov. Greg Abbott, the DGA’s minimal involvement in the race turned into a blistering wound that Hinojosa’s allies argued cut at the heart of the party’s historic lack of investment in Latino communities and candidates.

It’s made the Texas race the heart of an intra-party debate that’s only poised to explode ahead of 2028, when Latino voters will be central to any winning presidential coalition. And her allies are out to challenge Beshear’s party leadership potential, taking their shots arguing that the Texas victory is not his to claim.
“Andy Beshear is going to have to look at his playbook and understand that there was some pretty big missteps,” Stephanie Valencia, co-founder of Latino polling firm Equis Research, told POLITICO.

The DGA defended its involvement and Beshear’s leadership, touting the more than $1.4 million it spent in Texas, including paying for campaign expenses and staff on the ground to support Hinojosa. The organization noted it featured Hinojosa at multiple events hosted by governors to introduce candidates like her to national donors.

“We always believed in Gina and knew she could win,” Meghan Meehan-Draper, the DGA’s executive director, said in a statement. “The DGA was proud to support her campaign as its largest contributor, along with our $12 million investment in Latino outreach across multiple successful campaigns on the path to electing a majority of Democratic governors for the first time since 2010.”
But Hinojosa’s allies say it was about more than just money.

In its final months, the surprising viability of Hinojosa’s campaign sparked a stand-off between Latino consultants, organizations and members of Congress on one side, and the national Democratic gubernatorial campaign arm on the other, over how to invest in winning Latinos, a bloc of voters whose tendencies to swing between parties is redefining the political landscape.

The campaign itself is also taking a shot at the DGA and Beshear. Hinojosa’s win “was the result of a curiosity that too many people in the establishment are still scared to embrace,” campaign manager Amy Friedman wrote in a post-election memo obtained by POLITICO. “Even the Democratic Governors Association — the entity set up to literally help Democrats win — never believed she could.”

The DGA’s investments haven’t added up to any goodwill for Beshear from the Latino leaders and Hinojosa’s allies, who accuse the Kentucky governor of first ignoring and later forgoing a chance to put his full weight behind Hinojosa, who on Tuesday became the state’s first Latina governor.

“Don’t even get me started,” said Rebecca Katz of Fight Agency, which worked with Gina’s campaign and has been calling out Beshear on X . “[The DGA] underestimated her every step of the way. Not only did they not give [that much] to Gina, but they actively undermined her with other donors. It was outrageous.”

What Hinojosa’s campaign and allies saw as a generational opportunity to take a risk and flip Texas was met with deep skepticism and an even deeper lack of resources across an ever-growing map of competitive governor’s races in a blue wave year. Texas is among the most expensive states in the country to campaign in, and rallying donors to spend big on state-level races has long been a party problem. Abbott had a massive war chest of $105.7 million and the backing of Elon Musk, the world’s richest man, who poured nearly half a billion dollars into the midterms overall.

Dozens of Latino leaders, in two separate letters from September to October, pleaded with the DGA and Beshear to invest more in Hinojosa’s bid, at first asking for $10 million and later lowering it to $3 million. The calls for a massive influx of cash that could level the playing field fell on deaf ears until the final weeks of the campaign. On Sept. 29, Beshear called Hinojosa to commit $1 million from the DGA.

Playing out in the background was the looming 2028 Democratic presidential landscape, which had already shifted to heavily rely on Latino voters even before Texas entered the picture. Beshear is one of many Democrats considering a presidential run.
But other potential contenders jumped in forcefully to back Hinojosa, making her campaign into a mini 2028 proxy battle.

Arizona Sen. Ruben Gallego, who was among the signatories of the letters to the DGA, campaigned with her twice. Both California Gov. Gavin Newsom and Maryland Gov. Wes Moore contributed to her campaign or fundraised for her. And Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker not only helped fund the DGA itself, but separately pledged $1.2 million to Hinojosa in early October , after Beshear’s phone call with Hinojosa.
body_zh: 德克萨斯州奥斯汀——吉娜·伊诺霍萨的惊人胜利使德克萨斯州处于政治地震的震中——而余震可能会颠覆安迪·贝希尔的入主白宫之路。
几个月来，日益沮丧的伊诺霍萨盟友公开和私下向贝希尔担任主席的民主党州长协会施压，要求其帮助推动她冲过终点线，因为许多全国民主党人和捐助者仍保持观望。周二，伊诺霍萨在德克萨斯州州长官邸的竞选中占据主导地位，掀起了民主党在全国各地掌权的浪潮，其中包括推翻了唐纳德·特朗普总统赢得的六个州的州长职位。
与 POLITICO 交谈的拉丁裔特工感到自己是正确的，并在贝希尔可能竞选 2028 年总统之前将矛头转向贝希尔。
“他的总统竞选已经结束，”致力于在中期选举中争取拉丁裔选民的民主党工作人员塞尔吉奥·冈萨雷斯 (Sergio Gonzalez) 说。
曾担任前副总统卡马拉·哈里斯竞选团队高级助手的冈萨雷斯表示，贝希尔“没有像总统那样理解政治”，并且“在这一刻让拉丁裔选民、得克萨斯州选民和民主党人失望了”。
伊诺霍萨的竞选成为最终的失败者竞选活动——民主党几乎放弃了征服这个州的努力，她的团队押注来自日益保守的里奥格兰德河谷的一位候选人可能会赢得大批拉丁裔选民。许多全国民主党人私下认为伊诺霍萨没有机会。但随着公众民意调查显示她与三届共和党州长格雷格·阿博特的差距缩小，DGA 对竞选的最低限度参与变成了一个伤口，伊诺霍萨的盟友认为这是该党历史上缺乏对拉丁裔社区和候选人投资的核心。
这使得德克萨斯州的竞选成为党内辩论的核心，而这场辩论只会在 2028 年之前爆发，届时拉丁裔选民将成为任何获胜总统联盟的核心。她的盟友们正在挑战贝希尔的党内领导潜力，他们争辩说德克萨斯州的胜利不是他能宣称的。
拉丁裔民意调查公司 Equis Research 联合创始人斯蒂芬妮·瓦伦西亚 (Stephanie Valencia) 告诉《政治》杂志：“安迪·贝希尔必须审视他的剧本，明白其中存在一些相当大的失误。”
DGA 为其参与和 Beshear 的领导力进行了辩护，宣称其在德克萨斯州花费了超过 140 万美元，包括支付竞选费用和现场工作人员支持伊诺霍萨的费用。该组织指出，伊诺霍萨出席了州长主办的多次活动，向国家捐助者介绍像她这样的候选人。
“我们一直相信吉娜，并且知道她能够获胜，”DGA 执行董事梅根·米汉-德雷珀 (Meghan Meehan-Draper) 在一份声明中表示。 “DGA 很自豪能够作为最大的捐助者支持她的竞选活动，同时我们还投资了 1200 万美元，在多次成功的竞选活动中为拉丁裔外展活动提供支持，以实现自 2010 年以来首次选举出多数民主党州长。”
但伊诺霍萨的盟友表示，这不仅仅是金钱的问题。
在最后几个月，伊诺霍萨竞选活动令人惊讶的活力引发了一​​场对峙，一方是拉美裔顾问、组织和国会议员，另一方是全国民主党州长竞选部门，争论的焦点是如何投资赢得拉美裔选民，他们在政党之间摇摆不定的选民群体正在重新定义政治格局。
竞选活动本身也在攻击 DGA 和 Beshear。竞选经理艾米·弗里德曼(Amy Friedman)在《政治》杂志获得的一份选举后备忘录中写道，伊诺霍萨的胜利“是好奇心的结果，而当权者中有太多人仍然不敢接受这种好奇心”。 “即使是民主党州长协会——这个旨在帮助民主党获胜的实体——也不相信她能做到。”
DGA 的投资并没有增加拉丁裔领导人和伊诺霍萨盟友对贝希尔的任何善意，他们指责肯塔基州州长先是忽视，后来又放弃了全力支持伊诺霍萨的机会，伊诺霍萨于周二成为该州第一位拉丁裔州长。
“别让我开始，”Fight Agency 的丽贝卡·卡茨 (Rebecca Katz) 说道，该机构与吉娜的竞选团队合作，并一直在 X 上呼吁贝希尔。 “[DGA] 低估了她的每一步。他们不仅没有给吉娜[那么多]，而且还通过其他捐助者积极破坏她的利益。这太令人愤慨了。”
伊诺霍萨的竞选团队和盟友认为，这是一次冒险并颠覆德克萨斯州的世代机会，但遭到了深深的怀疑，在蓝色浪潮的一年里，竞争激烈的州长竞选地图上，资源的匮乏甚至更加严重。德克萨斯州是美国竞选成本最高的州之一，而召集捐助者在州级竞选上投入巨资长期以来一直是政党的一个问题。阿博特拥有 1.057 亿美元的巨额资金，并得到了世界首富埃隆·马斯克的支持，后者在中期选举中总共投入了近 5 亿美元。
数十名拉丁裔领导人在 9 月至 10 月期间分别写了两封信，恳求 DGA 和 Beshear 在伊诺霍萨的竞购中增加投资，最初要求 1000 万美元，后来降至 300 万美元。直到竞选的最后几周，有关大量现金流入以创造公平竞争环境的呼吁都被置若罔闻。 9 月 29 日，Beshear 致电 Hinojosa，要求其从 DGA 中拨款 100 万美元。
背景是迫在眉睫的 2028 年民主党总统选举格局，甚至在德克萨斯州加入之前，民主党总统选举就已经转向严重依赖拉丁裔选民。贝希尔是众多考虑竞选总统的民主党人之一。
但其他潜在竞争者纷纷大力支持伊诺霍萨，使她的竞选活动变成了一场小型的 2028 年代理权争夺战。
亚利桑那州参议员鲁本·加莱戈（Ruben Gallego）是给 DGA 信件的签署人之一，曾两次与她一起竞选。加利福尼亚州州长加文·纽瑟姆和马里兰州州长韦斯·摩尔都为她的竞选活动做出了贡献或为她筹款。伊利诺伊州州长 JB Pritzker 不仅为 DGA 本身提供了资金，还在 Beshear 与 Hinojosa 通电话后于 10 月初单独承诺向 Hinojosa 提供 120 万美元。

title_en: Democratic thrashing redraws the map of state power
title_zh: 民主斗争重新绘制国家权力版图
summary: Dems picked up more than 500 seats (and counting) and flipped at least 12 legislative chambers.
summary_zh: 民主党赢得了 500 多个席位（并且还在增加），并推翻了至少 12 个立法院。
body_en: The blue wave crashed through statehouses across the country Tuesday — carrying political and policy ramifications that will reverberate for years.

Democrats flipped more than 500 state legislative seats and won control of at least a dozen legislative chambers, establishing new governing trifectas in Michigan, Arizona, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, Wisconsin and Nevada. They captured legislative chambers in Texas, Georgia and North Carolina — states long dominated by Republican lawmakers. And they picked up even more legislative seats in deep blue strongholds like New York, California and Illinois.

The victories give Democrats an opening to pursue long-stalled agendas on housing costs and public education, along with new leverage in fights over taxing wealthy people and corporations and regulating artificial intelligence. Their gains will also reshape the country’s redistricting wars — and test whether Democrats can turn their backlash-fueled victories into changes voters can feel in their daily lives.

“We had a generational opportunity to shift the power in our states and to affect change and we did just that,” Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee President Heather Williams said. “ We ran the table. It's amazing.”

The scale of the victory is historic. In New York, Democrats are on track for their biggest state Senate majority since 1846, when they were running against the Whigs. In Texas, they won the state House for the first time since 2002. Arizona will have its first Democratic trifecta since the 1960s. And Democrats flipped Georgia's House, the first chamber Democrats have taken back in the Deep South in the modern era. Altogether, the party won more seats than in any year since the post-Watergate campaign of 1974.

The gains represent the most seismic change in state capitals since Republicans shellacked Democrats nationwide in 2010, picking up nearly 700 state legislative seats and flipping 20 chambers. They used that power in the ensuing years to entrench conservative policies and redraw legislative maps in their favor in wide swaths of the country.

Wisconsin Republicans, for example, swept every statewide office and won control of both legislative chambers that year, clearing the way to enact a far-reaching conservative agenda that remade the state over the ensuing decade. On Tuesday, Democrats flipped both legislative chambers.

“This is an incredible moment for the state of Wisconsin and the country,” said Wisconsin Assembly Minority Leader Greta Neubauer, who’s expected to become speaker next year. ”We are going to use this power to deliver for the people of our state and demonstrate that government can be a force for good in their lives and things are different when Democrats are in charge.”

Democrats have been steadily clawing their way back to power in state capitals in recent election cycles, including picking up 31 seats in special elections and Virginia’s 2025 legislative elections after Donald Trump returned to the White House. After Tuesday, they now control a narrow majority of at least 51 state legislative chambers, up from 29 when Trump first took office in 2016, according to the DLCC.

But newly empowered Democratic state lawmakers will face a challenging political and economic landscape with voters angry at elected officials of all partisan stripes as they face pocketbook woes and government failings.

Veteran Minnesota Republican strategist Gregg Peppin, who worked on state Senate races this cycle, said the results there largely hinged on what voters were most angry about: the state’s massive fraud scandals under Democratic governance, or a deeply unpopular president. Ultimately, Democrats padded their state Senate majority by five seats and won control of the House.

“Clearly we found out they were more fed up with Donald Trump than they were with fraud,” Peppin said. “Everybody’s just worn out from the guy, I think Republicans too. It’s just time to turn the page.”

In Arizona, Rep. Oscar De Los Santos, who’s poised to become speaker of the House when lawmakers reconvene in Phoenix next year, said they have a robust agenda planned given their long time in the political wilderness. “We have sixty years of pent-up ideas that we have not been able to move,” he said. “There's a bunch of legislation that we've got ready to go.”
Among the items on the agenda: banning corporate landlords from buying homes, cracking down on surveillance pricing based on people’s past purchases and addressing the state’s massive water woes.
De Los Santos said Democrats would crack down on Saudi-owned farms using Arizona water to grow alfalfa for export.

Another top target: reigning in the state’s universal education voucher program, which allows families to tap taxpayer dollars not only for private school tuition, but also for other education-related expenses. De Los Santos points out that public dollars have been used to pay for ski trips , kitchen remodels and even lingerie .

“It’s insane. It is out of control,” he said. “You've got literally thousands of dollars spent at Victoria's Secret from this program and so we're going to put an end to all of that nonsense and redirect those funds to our public schools.”

Democrats also juiced their majorities Tuesday in states where they already enjoyed governing trifectas. Republicans took a beating, for example, in Chicago’s suburbs, with Democrats flipping a string of state legislative seats — held by both moderates and conservatives — and further shrinking the GOP’s once-formidable presence in the region.

Republicans lost at least eight seats in the Illinois General Assembly, including six held by sitting lawmakers and two open seats. The drubbing further expands Democrats’ supermajorities in both chambers: They’ll now hold 84 out of 118 seats in the House and 45 out of 59 seats in the Senate.

“It means Democrats don’t have to try to work toward the middle [on legislation], which is really where the vast majority of the electorate is,” said state GOP Rep. Dan Ugaste, who represents Chicago’s far western suburbs and was among the Republicans who lost Tuesday.
body_zh: 周二，蓝色浪潮席卷了全国各地的州议会大厦，其政治和政策影响将持续数年。
民主党推翻了 500 多个州立法席位，赢得了至少十几个立法院的控制权，在密歇根州、亚利桑那州、宾夕法尼亚州、明尼苏达州、威斯康星州和内华达州建立了新的执政三连胜。他们占领了德克萨斯州、佐治亚州和北卡罗来纳州的立法厅，这些州长期由共和党议员主导。他们在纽约、加利福尼亚和伊利诺伊州等深蓝据点获得了更多立法席位。
这些胜利让民主党有机会追求长期停滞的住房成本和公共教育议程，并在对富人和企业征税以及监管人工智能的斗争中获得新的筹码。他们的成果也将重塑该国的选区重新划分战争，并考验民主党能否将其引发强烈反对的胜利转化为选民日常生活中能感受到的变化。
民主党立法竞选委员会主席希瑟·威廉姆斯说：“我们有一代人的机会来转移我们各州的权力并影响变革，我们就是这么做的。” “我们跑完了桌子。太棒了。”
这场胜利的规模是历史性的。在纽约，民主党有望获得自 1846 年与辉格党竞选以来最大的州参议院多数席位。在得克萨斯州，他们自 2002 年以来首次赢得州众议院席位。亚利桑那州将迎来 20 世纪 60 年代以来的首次民主党三连胜。民主党推翻了佐治亚州众议院，这是现代民主党在南方腹地夺回的第一议院。总的来说，该党赢得的席位比 1974 年水门事件后的任何一年都多。
这些进展是自2010年共和党在全国范围内猛烈抨击民主党、夺取近700个州立法席位并推翻20个众议院以来各州首府发生的最剧烈的变化。在接下来的几年里，他们利用这一权力巩固保守政策，并在全国大部分地区重新绘制有利于他们的立法地图。
例如，威斯康星州共和党人当年横扫了全州所有办公室，并赢得了两院的控制权，为制定影响深远的保守派议程扫清了道路，在接下来的十年里重塑了该州。周二，民主党推翻了两院。
“对于威斯康星州和整个国家来说，这是一个令人难以置信的时刻，”预计将于明年成为议长的威斯康星州议会少数党领袖格蕾塔·纽鲍尔 (Greta Neubauer) 说。 “我们将利用这一权力为我们州人民提供服务，并证明政府可以成为他们生活中的一股向善力量，而当民主党掌权时，情况就会有所不同。”
在最近的选举周期中，民主党一直在各州首府稳步夺回权力，包括在唐纳德·特朗普重返白宫后的特别选举和弗吉尼亚州 2025 年立法选举中获得 31 个席位。据 DLCC 称，周二之后，他们现在控制着至少 51 个州立法会的微弱多数，而特朗普 2016 年首次上任时，他们控制着 29 个州立法会。
但新获得权力的民主党州立法者将面临充满挑战的政治和经济形势，选民对所有党派的民选官员感到愤怒，因为他们面临着钱包问题和政府失误。
明尼苏达州资深共和党策略师格雷格·佩平(Gregg Peppin)参与了本周期的州参议院竞选，他表示，选举结果很大程度上取决于选民最愤怒的是什么：民主党治理下的该州大规模欺诈丑闻，或者是一位非常不受欢迎的总统。最终，民主党在州参议院的多数席位上增加了五个席位，并赢得了众议院的控制权。
“显然，我们发现他们更厌倦的是唐纳德·特朗普，而不是欺诈，”佩平说。 “每个人都对这个家伙感到厌倦了，我想共和党人也是如此。现在是翻开新页的时候了。”
在亚利桑那州，众议员奥斯卡·德洛斯桑托斯 (Oscar De Los Santos) 将于明年议员们在菲尼克斯再次召开会议时成为众议院议长，他表示，鉴于他们在政治荒野中长期处于政治荒野，他们已经计划了一个强有力的议程。 “我们有六十年被压抑的想法，但我们一直无法改变，”他说。 “我们已经准备好制定一系列立法。”
议程上的项目包括：禁止企业房东购买房屋、打击基于人们过去购买情况的监督定价以及解决该州巨大的水问题。
德洛斯桑托斯表示，民主党将打击沙特拥有的农场利用亚利桑那州的水种植苜蓿以供出口的行为。
另一个首要目标：控制该州的全民教育券计划，该计划允许家庭利用纳税人的钱不仅支付私立学校的学费，还可以支付其他与教育相关的费用。德洛斯桑托斯指出，公共资金被用来支付滑雪旅行、厨房改造甚至内衣的费用。
“这太疯狂了。它已经失控了，”他说。 “从这个项目中，你实际上已经在维多利亚的秘密花费了数千美元，因此我们将结束所有这些废话，并将这些资金重新分配给我们的公立学校。”
周二，民主党在已经获得三连胜的州也获得了多数席位。例如，共和党在芝加哥郊区遭到了打击，民主党推翻了一系列由温和派和保守派持有的州立法席位，并进一步削弱了共和党在该地区一度强大的影响力。
共和党在伊利诺伊州议会中失去了至少八个席位，其中包括现任议员占据的六个席位和两个空缺席位。此次惨败进一步扩大了民主党在参众两院的绝对多数席位：他们现在将在众议院 118 个席位中占据 84 个席位，在参议院 59 个席位中占据 45 个席位。
“这意味着民主党人不必试图在立法上向中间派努力，而这实际上是绝大多数选民的立场，”代表芝加哥远西郊区的州共和党众议员丹·乌加斯特(Dan Ugaste)说，他是周二落败的共和党人之一。

body_en: From the military to healthcare, Trump systematically dismantled Obama-era protections for transgender rights

Shelby Chestnut remembers turning on the news in 2016 and hearing something he didn’t expect. Then- attorney general, Loretta Lynch, had just announced a federal lawsuit to block HB2 in North Carolina , otherwise known as the “bathroom bill”. Lynch said the law, which made it illegal for transgender people to use a public restroom that did not align with the sex listed on their birth certificate, was reminiscent of those passed during the Jim Crow era that restricted public facility use by race. Then, she addressed transgender Americans directly: “But no matter how isolated or scared you may feel today, the Department of Justice and the entire Obama administration wants you to know that we see you; we stand with you; and we will do everything we can to protect you going forward.”
HB 2 was repealed within the year. Chestnut said he thought at the time: “Oh this is the next phase of protections for trans people.”
body_zh: 从军事到医疗保健，特朗普系统性地废除了奥巴马时代对变性人权利的保护

谢尔比·切斯特纳特 (Shelby Chestnut) 记得 2016 年打开新闻时听到了一些他没想到的内容。时任总检察长洛雷塔·林奇 (Loretta Lynch) 刚刚宣布提起联邦诉讼，以阻止北卡罗来纳州的 HB2，也称为“浴室法案”。林奇表示，这项法律规定变性人使用与出生证明上所列性别不相符的公共厕所是违法的，这让人想起种族隔离时代通过的那些限制种族使用公共设施的法律。然后，她直接对跨性别美国人说：“但无论你们今天感到多么孤立或害怕，司法部和整个奥巴马政府都希望你们知道，我们看到你们；我们与你们站在一起；我们将尽一切努力保护你们前进。”
HB 2 于年内被废除。切斯特纳特说，他当时想：“哦，这是保护跨性别者的下一阶段。”

title_en: Native American women made history in tribal, state and federal elections
title_zh: 美国原住民妇女在部落、州和联邦选举中创造了历史
summary: The election could have marked a turning point for Native American women.
summary_zh: 这次选举可能标志着美国原住民妇女的一个转折点。

The election could have marked a turning point for Native American women.
ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. -- A third-grade field trip to the Navajo Nation Council sparked Crystalyne Curley’s political ambition when she witnessed a fiery debate erupt between two tribal lawmakers.
“I thought to myself at a very young age, that’s where I want to be,” Curley said.
On Election Day, Curley surpassed that childhood dream and broke a barrier she says she never imagined as a nine-year-old: She was elected the first woman president of the Navajo Nation.

This week's elections brought a wave of milestone victories , from the nation’s first Black female governor to the first openly gay man and first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. It also marked a turning point for Native American women, whose leadership in their families and communities has rarely translated to formal political power.
Peggy Flanagan became the first Native American woman elected to the Senate, Deb Haaland the first to win a state governorship, and Curley the first to lead one of the largest tribes.
“This is a win for all Navajo women,” Curley told The Associated Press.

Jordan James Harvill, a Cherokee Nation citizen and strategist with the advocacy group Advance Native Political Leadership, said decades of political organizing are bearing fruit as more Native women run for and win office.
“This is a seismic shift that is happening in our communities,” he said.

Lene Bitsui supported Curley in the Navajo Nation election because she felt she was best positioned to restore order to the tribal government after what she sees as a period of dysfunction . But when Bitsui cast her ballot, she felt pessimistic.
“I thought our people weren't ready for a female president,” Bitsui said. “I was wrong, and I feel so happy to have been wrong.”

The modern, centralized Navajo government has been led by men since its establishment under federal pressure over a century ago. Navajo has the largest land base of any federally recognized tribe, spanning 27,000 square miles (70,000 square kilometers) in Arizona, New Mexico and Utah, and is second in population to the Cherokee Nation in Oklahoma.

Some Navajo people believe traditional teachings prohibit women from holding top government positions. Others say women's absence from the presidency stands in contrast to the matrilineal structure of Diné society.

“You see the language of tradition used to both deride the possibility of a woman being president and to say that women’s leadership is needed now,” said Jennifer Nez Denetdale, a professor of Diné studies at the University of New Mexico.

Curley, who narrowly defeated attorney Justin Jones, according to unofficial results, told the AP she faced sexist rhetoric while campaigning and expects to be held to a higher standard as the first woman president.

“As women, we have to work twice or triple as hard, especially within Navajo politics,” said Curley, who also was the first female to lead the tribe's legislative branch as speaker of the tribal council.

这次选举可能标志着美国原住民妇女的一个转折点。
新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基——三年级时，克里斯托琳·柯利 (Crystalyne Curley) 到纳瓦霍族议会进行实地考察，目睹了两名部落立法者之间爆发的激烈辩论，激发了她的政治野心。
“我在很小的时候就对自己说，这就是我想要成为的地方，”柯利说。
在选举日，柯利超越了儿时的梦想，打破了她说她九岁时从未想象过的障碍：她当选为纳瓦霍族第一位女总统。
本周的选举带来了一系列具有里程碑意义的胜利，从美国第一位黑人女州长到第一位公开同性恋身份的男子和第一位穆斯林当选美国参议院议员。这也标志着美国原住民妇女的一个转折点，她们在家庭和社区中的领导地位很少转化为正式的政治权力。
佩吉·弗拉纳根 (Peggy Flanagan) 成为第一位当选参议员的美国原住民女性，德布·哈兰德 (Deb Haaland) 成为第一位赢得州长职位的女性，而柯利 (Curley) 则是第一位领导最大部落之一的女性。
“这是所有纳瓦霍女性的胜利，”柯利告诉美联社。
切罗基原住民公民、倡导组织“推进原住民政治领导力”的战略家乔丹·詹姆斯·哈维尔表示，随着越来越多的原住民妇女竞选并赢得公职，数十年的政治组织正在取得成果。
“这是我们社区正在发生的翻天覆地的变化，”他说。
琳·比特苏 (Lene Bitsui) 在纳瓦霍族部落选举中支持柯利，因为她认为，在经历了一段失调时期后，她最有能力恢复部落政府的秩序。但当Bitsui投票时，她感到悲观。
“我认为我们的人民还没有准备好迎接一位女总统，”比特井说。 “我错了，我很高兴自己错了。”
现代集权的纳瓦霍政府自一个多世纪前在联邦压力下成立以来一直由男性领导。纳瓦霍拥有联邦承认的部落中最大的土地基地，占地 27,000 平方英里（70,000 平方公里），分布在亚利桑那州、新墨西哥州和犹他州，人口数量仅次于俄克拉荷马州的切罗基族。
一些纳瓦霍人认为，传统教义禁止女性担任政府高层职位。其他人则表示，女性担任总统的缺席与迪内社会的母系结构形成鲜明对比。
新墨西哥大学迪内研究教授詹妮弗·内兹·德内特代尔 (Jennifer Nez Denetdale) 表示：“你会看到传统语言既嘲笑女性担任总统的可能性，又说现在需要女性领导力。”
根据非官方结果，柯利以微弱优势击败了律师贾斯汀·琼斯，她告诉美联社，她在竞选期间面临性别歧视言论，并希望作为第一位女总统能够达到更高的标准。
“作为女性，我们必须付出两倍或三倍的努力，特别是在纳瓦霍政治中，”柯利说，她也是第一位担任部落议会发言人领导部落立法部门的女性。

Voters have sent a strong election-year message to President Donald Trump and the new Democratic congressional majority to repair the U.S. economy damaged by inflation
WASHINGTON -- Voters have sent a strong election-year message to the new Democratic congressional majority and President Donald Trump : Repair the damage inflation has done to the economy .

Trump, who campaigned on the idea that a Democratic victory in the midterms would trigger a 1929-style economic depression, has maintained that the economy is booming. Since his party lost in Tuesday's voting, he has claimed he is willing to work with Democrats in the House and Senate, though that's not something he has done much of in the past.
“I’ll get along, probably, with the Democrats, unless they want to be destructive,” Trump told reporters last week.

After Friday’s strong jobs report showed employers adding 165,000 jobs and the unemployment rate dipping to 4.1%, Trump was defiant. “Democrats may control Congress, but I will NEVER stop fighting for you, and I will VETO anything that hurts America,” he said in a text message to his supporters.

Democrats are seeking to check Trump's power and are preparing for early fights on government spending. Other challenges include chronic budget deficits, tariffs, artificial intelligence and difficult choices about a Social Security system that could run short of money in as little as six years .
But as long as rising prices keep making middle-class lives less affordable , Democrats and Republicans alike face the risk of angering and alienating voters in the next election cycle.

“Until inflation and interest rates are under control, the likelihood of change elections is going to be high on an ongoing basis,” said Marc Goldwein, senior vice president at the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget.

Trump's tariffs and the war against Iran that he launched in February contributed to the consumer price index climbing to 3.7% annually. The president also tried to bully the Federal Reserve , an independent body tasked with keeping inflation low, to slash its benchmark interest rate in ways that could have worsened inflation.

The gridlock of a Republican White House and Democratic Congress gives the Fed more room to maneuver, possibly smoothing the central bank's ability to return inflation to the 2% target it has failed to reach for nearly six years.
“I think that one of the surprise winners Tuesday was the Fed,” said Douglas Holtz-Eakin, an economist and president of the center-right American Action Forum.

The Democratic Senate could block Trump's ability to fill potentially open spots on the Fed board, Holtz-Eakin said, removing “Trump's incentives to meddle with the Fed” and clearing a path for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh “to follow his instincts and aggressively reduce inflation.”
Trump has maintained that the costs of oil, gasoline and diesel will all plummet once the Iran war ends. The problem is he refuses to say when or how the war will come to a conclusion.
John Cochrane, an economist at Stanford University's Hoover Institution, stressed that the Fed's efforts to combat inflation would be helped if the federal government reduced budget deficits.
“It takes monetary and fiscal restraint,” he said.

The U.S. government keeps amassing debt as tax revenues fall short of burgeoning spending on Medicare, Medicaid, Social Security and other programs. Paying the interest on the national debt now tops $1 trillion annually and exceeds spending on the military. The problem could spiral because investors have pushed up the interest rates charged on government debt over the past year.

华盛顿——选民们向新任民主党国会多数派和唐纳德·特朗普总统发出了选举年的强烈信息：修复通货膨胀对经济造成的损害。
特朗普在竞选时主张民主党在中期选举中获胜将引发 1929 年式的经济萧条，但他一直坚称经济正在蓬勃发展。自从他的政党在周二的投票中失利以来，他声称他愿意与众议院和参议院的民主党人合作，尽管他过去并没有做过很多事情。
特朗普上周对记者表示：“我可能会与民主党相处融洽，除非他们想具有破坏性。”
在周五强劲的就业报告显示雇主增加了 165,000 个就业岗位且失业率降至 4.1% 后，特朗普表现得目中无人。 “民主党人可能控制国会，但我永远不会停止为你们而战，我将否决任何伤害美国的事情，”他在给支持者的短信中说。
民主党人正在寻求遏制特朗普的权力，并为政府支出的早期斗争做好准备。其他挑战包括长期预算赤字、关税、人工智能以及社会保障体系的艰难选择，社会保障体系可能在短短六年内出现资金短缺。
但只要物价上涨继续让中产阶级的生活变得更加难以负担，民主党和共和党都将面临在下一个选举周期激怒和疏远选民的风险。
负责任联邦预算委员会高级副主席马克·戈德温表示：“在通胀和利率得到控制之前，变革选举的可能性将持续很高。”
特朗普的关税和他2月份发起的对伊朗战争导致消费者价格指数每年攀升至3.7%。总统还试图欺凌美联储这个负责保持低通胀的独立机构，以可能加剧通胀的方式大幅削减基准利率。
共和党白宫和民主党国会的僵局为美联储提供了更多回旋余地，可能会削弱央行将通胀率恢复到近六年来未能达到的 2% 目标的能力。
“我认为周二的意外赢家之一是美联储，”经济学家、中右翼美国行动论坛主席道格拉斯·霍尔茨-埃金 (Douglas Holtz-Eakin) 表示。
霍尔茨-埃金表示，民主党参议院可能会阻止特朗普填补美联储董事会潜在空缺职位的能力，从而消除“特朗普干预美联储的动机”，并为美联储主席凯文·沃什“跟随自己的直觉并积极降低通胀”扫清道路。
特朗普坚称，一旦伊朗战争结束，石油、汽油和柴油的成本将大幅下降。问题是他拒绝透露战争何时或如何结束。
斯坦福大学胡佛研究所经济学家约翰·科克伦强调，如果联邦政府减少预算赤字，将有助于美联储对抗通胀的努力。
“这需要货币和财政约束，”他说。
由于税收收入不足以满足医疗保险、医疗补助、社会保障和其他项目迅速增长的支出，美国政府不断积累债务。现在每年支付的国债利息超过 1 万亿美元，超过了军事开支。由于投资者在过去一年提高了政府债务利率，问题可能会加剧。
