body_en: Judge to appoint special master to determine whether Trump lawyers purposely misled her over golf course | Washington DC
Ana Reyes wants to know whether federal officials lied about extent of renovation plans at East Potomac golf course

A federal judge said on Saturday that she intended to appoint an ex-top federal prosecutor who served during Donald Trump’s first term to investigate whether she was purposely misled by lawyers and administration officials over changes to a historic public golf course in Washington DC .

Jessie Liu, a former US attorney for the District of Columbia, would examine whether officials with the interior department and the National Park Service and attorneys with the Department of Justice violated ethics or misled US district judge Ana Reyes during the course of the civil case that was initiated with a lawsuit in February by the DC Preservation League and two golfers.

The lawsuit challenges one of the US president’s flurry of construction projects around the nation’s capital – in this case, the renovation of a public golf facility along the Potomac River, which is less high-profile that some of his other plans but had still riled many.

The Republican administration plans to close the East Potomac golf course and park on 15 November with the intention of constructing what it has called a “World Class, championship-level golf course that is capable of hosting major events”.

An injunction issued by Reyes last month temporarily bars the government from removing or damaging any additional trees on the course and ordered the administration to give 10 days’ notice in writing before making any “irreparable modification” to any “forms or features” of the course while the lawsuit is active.

Reyes is now giving each side a chance to be heard on her plan to name Liu as special master in the case. They must do so in writing by Friday, when the next court hearing in the dispute is scheduled.
Reyes, who was nominated by Joe Biden during his term, wants to know whether federal officials lied about the extent of renovation plans during prior months of hearings.
She also demands to know whether they were truthful about various steps they took, including cutting down hundreds of trees early last month.

Reyes announced during a hearing on 30 October that she was starting a formal investigation into the government’s conduct. Earlier in the case, she had rejected numerous motions from the plaintiffs to step in, saying she trusted the government attorneys.

As the city’s then chief federal prosecutor, Liu oversaw some of the matters referred to her office by then-special counsel Robert Mueller during his investigation into alleged ties between Trump’s 2016 election campaign and Russia .

Trump later nominated her to be associate attorney general, the third-highest-ranking justice department job. Liu withdrew from consideration after running into opposition on the Republican-led Senate judiciary committee because of her past membership in a lawyers’ group that had supported abortion rights.

David Super, a law professor at the Georgetown University law center, said the initiation of a formal investigation by a judge to look into the conduct of a trial’s participants “can be a precursor to holding someone in contempt of court”.

Super said it also is a reflection “of the difficulty she had in determining who initiated the tree-cutting in defiance of the assurances DoJ provided. She doesn’t have the time to keep holding long, complex hearings and so wants a special master to narrow the issues.”

Meanwhile, on Saturday afternoon, Trump posted a long and outlandish message on his social media platform declaring that he was “ordering” the justice department immediately to “look into” Democrats whom he said were “threatening” people in his administration with impeachment, referring to such suggested conduct as a “criminal act”.

The garbled post also accused Democrats of threatening Republican donors and called out the Michigan US senator Elissa Slotkin, a Democrat, saying she was “going after” young people who “give even the slightest inclination to be a Republican” and that this amounted to extortion. The US president did not present further detail or explanation of his claims.

安娜·雷耶斯想知道联邦官员是否对东波托马克高尔夫球场的改造计划撒了谎
一名联邦法官周六表示，她打算任命一名在唐纳德·特朗普第一任期内任职的前联邦高级检察官，调查她是否因华盛顿特区一座历史悠久的公共高尔夫球场的改变而被律师和政府官员故意误导。
哥伦比亚特区前美国检察官杰西·刘(Jessie Liu)将调查内政部和国家公园管理局的官员以及司法部的律师在华盛顿保护联盟和两名高尔夫球手于二月份提起的民事案件过程中是否违反道德或误导美国地区法官安娜·雷耶斯(Ana Reyes)。
这起诉讼对美国总统在首都周边的一系列建设项目之一提出了挑战——在本案中，是对波托马克河沿岸一个公共高尔夫设施的改造，该项目不像他的其他一些计划那么引人注目，但仍然激怒了许多人。
共和党政府计划于11月15日关闭东波托马克高尔夫球场和公园，目的是建设一个所谓的“能够举办重大赛事的世界级、锦标赛级高尔夫球场”。
雷耶斯上个月发布的一项禁令暂时禁止政府移除或损坏球场上的任何其他树木，并命令管理部门在诉讼进行期间，在对球场的任何“形式或功能”进行任何“不可挽回的修改”之前，提前 10 天发出书面通知。
雷耶斯现在让双方都有机会听取她任命刘作为此案特别主审的计划。他们必须在周五之前以书面形式提出，届时该纠纷的下一次法庭听证会将会安排。
雷耶斯在任期内由乔·拜登提名，他想知道联邦官员在前几个月的听证会上是否对翻修计划的范围撒了谎。
她还要求知道他们所采取的各种措施是否属实，包括上月初砍伐了数百棵树。
雷耶斯在 10 月 30 日的听证会上宣布，她将开始对政府的行为进行正式调查。在此案早些时候，她拒绝了原告提出的多项介入动议，称她信任政府律师。
作为该市时任首席联邦检察官，刘负责监督时任特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒(Robert Mueller)在调查特朗普2016年竞选活动与俄罗斯之间涉嫌关系期间向其办公室转交的一些事务。
特朗普后来提名她担任副司法部长，这是司法部排名第三的职位。刘因过去是支持堕胎权的律师团体的成员，在共和党领导的参议院司法委员会遭到反对后退出了考虑。
乔治城大学法律中心的法学教授大卫·苏珀表示，法官启动正式调查以调查审判参与者的行为“可能是判定某人藐视法庭的先兆”。
超级说，这也反映出“她在确定谁发起了砍伐树木的行为时遇到了困难，无视司法部提供的保证。她没有时间继续举行漫长而复杂的听证会，因此希望有一位特别的大师来缩小问题范围。”
与此同时，周六下午，特朗普在他的社交媒体平台上发布了一条长而古怪的信息，宣称他正在“命令”司法部立即“调查”民主党人，他称这些民主党人用弹劾“威胁”他的政府人员，并将此类建议的行为称为“犯罪行为”。
这篇乱码帖子还指责民主党威胁共和党捐助者，并指责美国密歇根州民主党参议员埃丽莎·斯洛特金(Elissa Slotkin)，称她正在“追捕”那些“哪怕有一丝一毫成为共和党倾向”的年轻人，这相当于敲诈勒索。美国总统没有提供进一步的细节或解释他的说法。

title_en: Republican consultant discusses what went wrong and what's next for the GOP
title_zh: 共和党顾问讨论出了什么问题以及共和党的下一步行动
summary: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe speaks to Hogan Gidley, a Republican consultant and former White House Deputy Press Secretary during the first Trump administration, about the GOP's post-midterm strategy.
summary_zh: NPR 的阿耶莎·拉斯科 (Ayesha Rascoe) 与特朗普第一届政府期间的共和党顾问、前白宫副新闻秘书霍根·吉德利 (Hogan Gidley) 进行了交谈
body_en: Republican consultant discusses what went wrong and what's next for the GOP NPR's Ayesha Rascoe speaks to Hogan Gidley, a Republican consultant and former White House Deputy Press Secretary during the first Trump administration, about the GOP's post-midterm strategy.
NPR's Ayesha Rascoe speaks to Hogan Gidley, a Republican consultant and former White House Deputy Press Secretary during the first Trump administration, about the GOP's post-midterm strategy.

January 20, 2025, was a blustery, bitterly cold day in Washington. President Trump, in his inaugural address, heralded a tide of change sweeping the country, thanking Black and Hispanic voters in particular. Less than two years later, another tide has swept in the opposite direction, electing Democrats in Republican strongholds from South Carolina to Kansas. So what went wrong for the GOP? And what's next for the party?
We're joined now by Hogan Gidley. He's a longtime Republican consultant, and he was White House deputy press secretary during the first Trump administration. Hogan, thanks for being here.
HOGAN GIDLEY: Great to be with you. Thanks so much for the time.
RASCOE: What happened to that expanded MAGA coalition that we mentioned? Why did Hispanics and young people, even young white men, turn away from the GOP?

GIDLEY: Polling suggests that their anger at the war and that their anger at prices had a lot to do with the way they voted. Because a lot of the things the Trump administration did - from no tax on tips to no tax on overtime and no tax on Social Security, doubling the child tax credit, the lowest number in crime we've seen over a century, the highest wages we've seen, the lowest number of unemployment we've ever seen - all those things are very exciting. Those things the American people like. What they didn't like were the war and prices.

RASCOE: Well, does Trump need to make any changes in his behavior? Because people are not happy with the direction of the country. They do not feel like Trump cares about their individual problems. So does Trump need to make any changes?

GIDLEY: Well, I'll tell you something that stood out to me that may answer this question. The mere fact that Donald Trump got elected to the White House and has been the driving force in politics for 10 years, based on the fact that he is the one who is viewed by the American people to be listening to them finally after decades of government officials and candidates and officeholders not listening to them - someone who was known to be the voice of the American people - the fact that that has shifted in their opinion and their perception is something that they'll have to address. How that looks moving forward, though, I think, is that there will be a massive - and this is my silver lining from the election - a massive overreach by Democrats and a misread of what the American people truly want from this last election.
RASCOE: Well, it sounds like what you're saying is that Republicans have to depend on missteps by Democrats. But what is the Republican plan? What is the...
GIDLEY: I think that's what's being formulated. It's...
RASCOE: Would you agree that they're a bit in the wilderness and they have to figure a way out?

GIDLEY: I wouldn't say they're in the wilderness. I'd say they're on the edge of the forest, wondering, what do we need to do before we step out into the field? Because they have the White House right now. They are in control of that. So it's obvious the American people still want Republicans to have some say. The question is - what are they saying, and how are they saying it? Democrats didn't run on anything other than being against Donald Trump. What's their agenda? I don't know what their agenda is either.

RASCOE: There's been a backlash to some of President Trump's immigration enforcement policies. Now the architect of Trump's immigration push, Stephen Miller, has been elevated to White House chief of staff. What does that tell you?

GIDLEY: It tells me that the administration wants to make sure that continuity is key heading into one of the most tumultuous times, most likely in our nation's history, because we face an onslaught of a weaponized Congress the likes of which we have never seen in this country against Donald Trump, with hoax after hoax, with impeachment attempt after impeachment attempt. They're going to continue to move that onslaught against Donald Trump and his administration. Stephen Miller was part and parcel with defending Donald Trump in the first term, as was I. And so Stephen's ready for that type of fight.

RASCOE: But what does that say to Latinos, who swung 21 points toward Democratic House candidates? And part of that, when you look at polls, was because of unmet promises to lower prices and because of the deportation tactics.
GIDLEY: I've not seen any indication of deportation tactics being the driving cause...
body_zh: 共和党顾问讨论共和党出了什么问题以及下一步该做什么 NPR 的阿伊莎·拉斯科 (Ayesha Rascoe) 与共和党顾问、特朗普第一届政府期间的前白宫新闻副秘书霍根·吉德利 (Hogan Gidley) 谈论了共和党的中期战略。
NPR 的阿伊莎·拉斯科 (Ayesha Rascoe) 与共和党顾问、特朗普第一届政府期间的前白宫副新闻秘书霍根·吉德利 (Hogan Gidley) 谈论了共和党的中期战略。
2025 年 1 月 20 日，华盛顿刮风，天气寒冷。特朗普总统在就职演说中预示着一场席卷全国的变革浪潮，特别感谢黑人和西班牙裔选民。不到两年后，另一股浪潮向相反的方向席卷而来，从南卡罗来纳州到堪萨斯州的共和党据点选举了民主党人。那么共和党出了什么问题呢？派对的下一步是什么？
霍根·吉德利现在加入我们。他是一名长期的共和党顾问，并在特朗普第一届政府期间担任白宫副新闻秘书。霍根，谢谢你来到这里。
霍根·吉德利：很高兴和你在一起。非常感谢您抽出时间。
拉斯科：我们提到的扩大 MAGA 联盟发生了什么？为什么西班牙裔和年轻人，甚至年轻的白人，都背弃了共和党？
吉德利：民意调查表明，他们对战争的愤怒和对物价的愤怒与他们的投票方式有很大关系。因为特朗普政府做了很多事情——从小费不征税到加班不征税、社会保障不征税、儿童税收抵免加倍、一个多世纪以来犯罪率最低、工资最高、失业率最低——所有这些事情都非常令人兴奋。那些美国人民喜欢的东西。他们不喜欢的是战争和物价。
拉斯科：那么，特朗普需要改变他的行为吗？因为人们对国家的方向不满意。他们不觉得特朗普关心他们的个人问题。那么特朗普需要做出什么改变吗？

吉德利：好吧，我会告诉你一些对我来说很突出的事情，也许可以回答这个问题。唐纳德·特朗普当选入主白宫，并在过去十年里一直是政治的推动力量，这一事实是基于这样一个事实：在政府官员、候选人和公职人员几十年来不听美国人民的意见之后，他最终被美国人民视为倾听他们的声音——他被认为是美国人民的声音——这一事实已经改变了他们的观点和看法，这是他们必须解决的问题。不过，我认为，未来的情况是，民主党将出现大规模的过度扩张，以及对美国人民从上次选举中真正想要的东西的误读，这是我从这次选举中看到的一线希望。
拉斯科：嗯，听起来你的意思是共和党必须依赖民主党的失误。但共和党的计划是什么？什么是...
吉德利：我认为这就是正在制定的内容。它是...
拉斯科：你是否同意他们有点陷入荒野并且必须找到出路？
吉德利：我不会说他们在荒野里。我想说他们在森林边缘，想知道在踏入野外之前我们需要做什么？因为他们现在拥有白宫。他们掌控着这一点。所以很明显美国人民仍然希望共和党有发言权。问题是 - 他们在说什么以及他们是如何说的？民主党人除了反对唐纳德·特朗普之外没有其他任何目的。他们的议程是什么？我也不知道他们的议程是什么。
拉斯科：特朗普总统的一些移民执法政策遭到了强烈反对。现在，特朗普移民计划的设计师斯蒂芬·米勒已被提升为白宫办公厅主任。这告诉你什么？

吉德利：它告诉我，政府希望确保连续性是进入我们国家历史上最动荡的时代之一的关键，因为我们面临着武器化的国会的攻击，这是我们在这个国家从未见过的针对唐纳德·特朗普的攻击，一个又一个的骗局，一个又一个的弹劾尝试。他们将继续对唐纳德·特朗普及其政府发起攻击。斯蒂芬·米勒（Stephen Miller）在第一任期中为唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）辩护，我也是如此。因此，斯蒂芬·米勒（Stephen Miller）已经为这种类型的战斗做好了准备。
拉斯科：但这对拉丁裔来说意味着什么呢？他们的支持率向民主党众议院候选人倾斜了 21 个百分点？从民意调查来看，部分原因是降价承诺未兑现，以及驱逐策略。
吉德利：我没有看到任何迹象表明驱逐策略是驱动因素......

title_en: Historically red state legislatures have flipped. Here's what's on their agenda
title_zh: 历史上的红色州立法机构已经翻转。这是他们的议程
summary: Democrats made sweeping gains in state legislatures across the country. We look at North Carolina and Arizona to see what that could mean.
summary_zh: 民主党在全国各州立法机构中取得了压倒性的胜利。我们看看北卡罗来纳州和亚利桑那州，看看这意味着什么。
body_en: Historically red state legislatures have flipped. Here's what's on their agenda Democrats made sweeping gains in state legislatures across the country. We look at North Carolina and Arizona to see what that could mean.
Democrats made sweeping gains in state legislatures across the country. We look at North Carolina and Arizona to see what that could mean.

Democrats made sweeping gains in state legislatures around the country, and they'll be looking to reverse recent history. In 2010, Republicans dominated state elections and used that power to advance their agenda for over a decade. So what are Democrats going to do this time around? We're going to hear from two of those states now, from two of our member stations with Colin Campbell of WUNC in North Carolina and Wayne Schutsky of KJZZ in Arizona. Welcome.
RASCOE: Both your states have had Democratic governors and heavily Republican legislatures. Let's start in North Carolina. Colin, what's changed there?

CAMPBELL: So Republicans here have had what they call working supermajorities for much of the past decade. That's enough votes, sometimes with the help of a Democrat or two, to override most of the Democratic governors' vetoes. That's allowed them to pass new abortion restrictions after the fall of Roe v. Wade, expand private school vouchers and also gerrymander congressional maps.

But on Tuesday, Democrats not only flipped the state House but will have a comfortable majority in that chamber. In the Senate, there's still one election that's being counted - could be just a one-seat majority for the GOP or a tie. If it's a tie, that would be broken by the Democratic lieutenant governor.
RASCOE: So what could change for North Carolinians? What are Democrats hoping to do?

CAMPBELL: You know, if Democrats manage to control both chambers, that could mean a rollback of abortion restrictions or reversing power grabs that have weakened the governor's office, and a whole lot more. If the Democrats end up coming up short in the state Senate, we get divided government, and it's unclear what, if anything, gets done. Regardless of how it shakes out, Democratic Governor Josh Stein is already calling for lawmakers from both parties to cooperate on issues like affordability.

JOSH STEIN: What I heard from the people of North Carolina is, do something for us, focus on our issues, listen to our concerns and work together. Don't be so focused on the partisan divide. Focus on producing for people.
CAMPBELL: A lot of the North Carolina voters I've talked with want to see that bipartisan progress.
RASCOE: Now to Wayne Schutsky in Phoenix. Bigger change there - Republicans had controlled both chambers of the legislature, but now it's a Democratic trifecta.

SCHUTSKY: That's right. With Democratic Governor Katie Hobbs easily winning reelection, Democrats will now hold both legislative chambers and the governor's office for the first time since 1966. And this was really part of that larger blue wave we saw across the country. I mean, just for example, not in the legislature, but even the Republican clerk of court in Maricopa County, the biggest county in the state, lost to a 19-year-old Democrat who's a philosophy student at ASU, who will now oversee hundreds of court employees.

So for years, the Republican-controlled legislature has blocked Hobbs, the Democratic governor, on her agenda, and she spent the last four decades playing defense, setting a state record with more than 500 vetoes. But now she'll be able to actually initiate changes that she wants to see in the state.
RASCOE: And what kind of changes are Democrats considering?

SCHUTSKY: Well, for years, Hobbs has tried to provide financial relief to Arizonans through things like rent and utility assistance, relief for first-time homebuyers, and increasing the amount the state spends to help families afford childcare. For instance, she sought around a hundred million to help with childcare assistance but only got a fraction of that, and we still have over 15,000 kids on the wait list for that program.

One thing we do know Democrats are going to do is try and crack down on Arizona's school voucher program, which is one of the biggest in the country. She sought to scale it back for years, as we've seen reports on families using public dollars for non-education items, things like jewelry and even lingerie. So this has been a huge issue, and Senate Republican John Kavanagh actually acknowledged to me in an interview that his party missed an opportunity to address some concerns about those vouchers, which we call ESAs here.
JOHN KAVANAGH: I think that in the area of, like, ESA reform, that was something that the voters very much wanted and that we weren't going along. I mean, that's one area that was problematic.
body_zh: 历史上的红色州立法机构已经翻转。以下是民主党在全国各州立法机构中取得压倒性胜利的议程。我们看看北卡罗来纳州和亚利桑那州，看看这意味着什么。
民主党在全国各州立法机构中取得了压倒性的胜利。我们看看北卡罗来纳州和亚利桑那州，看看这意味着什么。

民主党在全国各地的州立法机构中取得了压倒性的胜利，他们将寻求扭转近期的历史。 2010 年，共和党在州选举中占据主导地位，并在十多年来利用这一权力推进他们的议程。那么民主党这次会做什么呢？我们现在将收到其中两个州的来信，即我们的两个会员电台的来信，即北卡罗来纳州 WUNC 的科林·坎贝尔 (Colin Campbell) 和亚利桑那州 KJZZ 的韦恩·舒茨基 (Wayne Schutsky)。欢迎。
拉斯科：你们两个州都有民主党州长和共和党占多数的立法机构。让我们从北卡罗来纳州开始。科林，那里有什么变化吗？
坎贝尔：所以，在过去十年的大部分时间里，这里的共和党人拥有他们所谓的“工作绝对多数”。这足以推翻大多数民主党州长的否决，有时还需要一两个民主党人的帮助。这使得他们能够在罗伊诉韦德案失败后通过新的堕胎限制、扩大私立学校的学券以及不公正地划分国会地图。
但周二，民主党不仅推翻了州众议院，而且将在众议院获得轻松的多数席位。在参议院，还有一项选举正在统计中——共和党可能只获得一个席位多数，也可能是平局。如果是平局，民主党副州长将打破这一局面。
拉斯科：那么北卡罗来纳州人会发生什么变化呢？民主党希望做什么？
坎贝尔：你知道，如果民主党成功控制参众两院，这可能意味着堕胎限制的回滚或扭转削弱州长办公室的权力争夺，等等。如果民主党最终在州参议院席位不足，我们的政府就会出现分裂，而且还不清楚我们会做什么（如果有的话）。无论结果如何，民主党州长乔什·斯坦（Josh Stein）已经呼吁两党立法者在负担能力等问题上进行合作。
乔什·斯坦：我从北卡罗来纳州人民那里听到的是，为我们做点什么，关注我们的问题，倾听我们的担忧并共同努力。不要太关注党派分歧。专注于为人民生产。
坎贝尔：我采访过的许多北卡罗来纳州选民都希望看到两党取得进展。
拉斯科：现在请凤凰城的韦恩·舒茨基发言。更大的变化是——共和党控制了立法机构的参众两院，但现在是民主党三连胜。
舒茨基：没错。随着民主党州长凯蒂·霍布斯 (Katie Hobbs) 轻松赢得连任，民主党将自 1966 年以来首次同时占据立法议会和州长职位。这确实是我们在全国各地看到的更大蓝色浪潮的一部分。我的意思是，举个例子，不是在立法机关，就连该州最大的县马里科帕县的共和党法院书记员也输给了一位 19 岁的民主党人，他是亚利桑那州立大学的哲学系学生，现在将管理数百名法院员工。
因此，多年来，共和党控制的立法机构一直将民主党州长霍布斯排除在她的议程之外，而她在过去四十年里一直在进行辩护，创下了超过 500 票否决的州纪录。但现在她将能够真正发起她希望在该州看到的变革。
拉斯科：民主党正在考虑什么样的改变？
舒茨基：多年来，霍布斯一直试图通过租金和公用事业援助、首次购房者减免以及增加州政府支出来帮助家庭负担儿童保育费用等方式为亚利桑那州人民提供经济援助。例如，她寻求了大约一亿美元的儿童保育援助，但只得到了其中的一小部分，而且我们仍有超过 15,000 名孩子在该计划的等待名单上。
我们确实知道民主党要做的一件事是尝试打击亚利桑那州的学校券计划，该计划是该国最大的计划之一。多年来，她一直试图缩减开支，因为我们看到有报道称，一些家庭将公共资金用于非教育物品、珠宝甚至内衣等。所以这是一个大问题，参议院共和党人约翰·卡瓦纳实际上在接受采访时向我承认，他的政党错过了解决对这些代金券（我们在这里称之为 ESA）的一些担忧的机会。
约翰·卡瓦纳：我认为在欧空局改革等领域，这是选民非常希望的事情，但我们没有同意。我的意思是，这是一个有问题的领域。

title_en: California's fifth consecutive Catholic governor exemplifies the faith's deep roots
title_zh: 加州连续第五任天主教州长体现了信仰的深厚根基
summary: Xavier Becerra's recent election as California governor highlights the state's unique blend of Catholicism and progressive politics
summary_zh: 泽维尔·贝塞拉 (Xavier Becerra) 最近当选为加州州长，凸显了该州天主教与进步政治的独特融合
body_en: Election 2026 live updates: Trump says US took 'giant step back' through midterms
Blanche says 'there could be' investigations of Dems pushing oversight probes
Trump says US took 'giant step back' through midterm results
Xavier Becerra's recent election as California governor highlights the state's unique blend of Catholicism and progressive politics

LOS ANGELES -- As he campaigned for California governor, Xavier Becerra reflected on the way his Catholic upbringing informs his politics. “The sanctity of life is something that’s really ingrained in you,” the Democrat and former U.S. health and human services secretary said earlier this year.

He then explained his rationale, confounding to some, for supporting abortion rights. Becerra exemplifies how Catholicism’s deep roots often go hand in hand with California’s progressive reputation. That complexity is a snapshot of a larger reality — that American Catholics are in many ways a politically mixed bag.

“There is no Catholic vote,” said David Gibson, the director of Fordham University’s Center on Religion and Culture. White evangelicals for Republicans or Black Protestants for Democrats are more politically reliable religious groups, he said.

With Becerra’s win this week, California has elected five consecutive Catholic governors — a remarkable streak indicative of Catholicism’s enduring influence. “Catholicism is part of the fabric of California culture the way Puritan Protestantism is part of the New England regions,” Gibson said.
Catholic voters — especially Latinos — helped elect Becerra, according to The AP Voter Poll , a survey of roughly 100,000 midterm voters. He became the state's first elected Latino governor.

Beginning with Gray Davis, who took office in 1999, four of those five governors also have been Democrats. Some have been more vocal about their faith than others — notably Jerry Brown, who was a seminarian in the 1950s.

California is home to more Catholics than any other U.S. state. A Pew Research Center poll in 2024 found that 25% of adults in California identify as Catholic, accounting for almost half of the state’s Christians.
But numbers aside, Catholicism has been woven into the fabric of the state for centuries.

From economically progressive strains of Catholic social teaching and explicit rejections of the death penalty to official teachings against abortion and in vitro fertilization, Catholic theology rarely fits neatly into political categories, which helps explain the unpredictable voting habits.

Take Gov. Gavin Newsom , whose strong support of abortion rights is at odds with Catholic leadership. Yet his announcement this week that he planned to change more than 500 death sentences in the state to life in prison without the possibility of parole was celebrated by the California Catholic Conference, the public policy organization representing the church in California.

“I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us,” Newsom said in a public letter.

Some leaders within the church have subverted Trump administration policies, like San Bernardino Bishop Alberto Rojas, who last year formally excused parishioners from their weekly obligation to attend Mass following immigration detentions on parish properties in the diocese.

Others have taken high-profile conservative stances, like San Francisco Archbishop Salvatore Cordileone, who in 2022 barred U.S. Rep. Nancy Pelosi, a Catholic, from receiving Communion over her support of abortion rights.

About 2 in 10 voters in the California governor’s race were Catholic, and they mostly voted for Becerra, according to The AP Voter Poll. About 6 in 10 Catholic voters supported Becerra, while about 4 in 10 voted for his Republican opponent Steve Hilton.
About 7 in 10 Latino Catholics voted for Becerra, while white Catholics were split between Becerra and Hilton.

特朗普称美国在中期选举结果中“大幅倒退”
泽维尔·贝塞拉 (Xavier Becerra) 最近当选为加州州长，凸显了该州天主教与进步政治的独特融合
洛杉矶——在竞选加州州长时，泽维尔·贝塞拉反思了自己的天主教成长经历对他的政治影响的方式。 “生命的神圣性是一种根深蒂固的东西，”这位民主党人、前美国卫生与公众服务部长今年早些时候表示。
然后他解释了他支持堕胎权的理由，这让一些人感到困惑。贝塞拉体现了天主教的深厚根基往往与加州进步的声誉紧密相连。这种复杂性是一个更大现实的缩影——美国天主教徒在很多方面都是政治上的混杂体。
“没有天主教徒的投票，”福特汉姆大学宗教与文化中心主任大卫·吉布森说。他说，共和党的白人福音派或民主党的黑人新教徒是政治上更可靠的宗教团体。
随着贝塞拉本周的胜利，加州连续选举出五位天主教州长——这一显着的连胜表明了天主教的持久影响力。 “天主教是加州文化的一部分，就像清教徒新教是新英格兰地区的一部分一样，”吉布森说。
根据美联社选民民意调查（对大约 10 万中期选民进行的调查），天主教选民，尤其是拉丁裔选民，帮助贝塞拉当选。他成为该州第一位当选的拉丁裔州长。
从1999年上任的格雷·戴维斯开始，这五位州长中有四位是民主党人。有些人比其他人更直言不讳地表达自己的信仰，尤其是 20 世纪 50 年代的神学院学生杰里·布朗 (Jerry Brown)。
加利福尼亚州的天主教徒人数比美国任何其他州都多。皮尤研究中心 2024 年的一项民意调查发现，加州 25% 的成年人是天主教徒，几乎占该州基督徒的一半。
但撇开数字不谈，几个世纪以来天主教已经融入到国家的结构中。
从天主教社会教义的经济进步和对死刑的明确拒绝，到反对堕胎和体外受精的官方教义，天主教神学很少完全符合政治范畴，这有助于解释不可预测的投票习惯。
以州长加文·纽瑟姆 (Gavin Newsom) 为例，他对堕胎权的强烈支持与天主教领导层不一致。然而，他本周宣布计划将该州 500 多名死刑判决改为终身监禁且不得假释，这一消息受到代表加州教会的公共政策组织加州天主教会议的庆祝。
纽瑟姆在一封公开信中表示：“我采取这一行动是因为我坚信，国家批准的杀戮与加州的价值观不相容，破坏了我们法律体系的基础，并削弱了我们每个人的能力。”
教会内的一些领导人颠覆了特朗普政府的政策，比如圣贝纳迪诺主教阿尔贝托·罗哈斯(Alberto Rojas)，他去年在教区教区财产上移民被拘留后，正式免除教区居民每周参加弥撒的义务。
其他人则采取了高调的保守立场，例如旧金山大主教萨尔瓦多·科迪莱昂 (Salvatore Cordileone)，由于天主教徒美国众议员南希·佩洛西 (Nancy Pelosi) 支持堕胎权，他于 2022 年禁止她接受圣餐。
据美联社选民民意调查显示，在加州州长竞选中，大约十分之二的选民是天主教徒，他们大多投票给贝塞拉。大约十分之六的天主教选民支持贝塞拉，而大约十分之四的人投票给他的共和党对手史蒂夫·希尔顿。
大约十分之七的拉丁裔天主教徒投票支持贝塞拉，而白人天主教徒则分为贝塞拉和希尔顿。

title_en: ‘We feel the love’: Epstein survivors overwhelmed by messages of support at pop-up art exhibition
title_zh: “我们感受到爱”：爱泼斯坦幸存者在快闪艺术展上被支持信息淹没
summary: Visitors to a touring show drawing attention to Epstein’s crimes have left thousands of ‘powerful’ notes – and survivors say it means a great deal When Danielle Bensky first went to The Donald J Trump and Jeffrey Epstein Memorial Reading Room, she didn’t know
summary_zh: 一场引起人们对爱泼斯坦罪行关注的巡回演出的参观者留下了数千条“有力”的笔记——幸存者表示，这意义重大。
body_en: Visitors to a touring show drawing attention to Epstein’s crimes have left thousands of ‘powerful’ notes – and survivors say it means a great deal
When Danielle Bensky first went to The Donald J Trump and Jeffrey Epstein Memorial Reading Room, she didn’t know what to expect.

“What happens if I walk in and survivors’ names are just plastered everywhere?” Bensky wondered about the reading room, a traveling exhibition of Epstein investigative files, first held in a New York City gallery this May. “I was a little worried in the beginning that this would be a form of exploitation for survivors.

The reading room is meant to bring attention to Epstein’s crimes and law enforcement’s decades-long failure to act. The former financier, who counted numerous high-profile men among his associates, was arrested in 2019 for sexual abuse of teen girls but killed himself in jail.

While Ghislaine Maxwell was arrested and found guilty of luring teen girls into Epstein’s orbit, documents reveal that law enforcement officials were well aware of their crimes decades prior. Survivors have called for greater transparency and legal actions against any other participants in their sexual abuse.

Bensky also didn’t know what would happen when David Garrett, founder of event organizer the Institute for Primary Facts , floated an idea to make the exhibit more interactive. There was a cork board in the final room and Garrett told Bensky he was going to keep it there when this exhibition opened to the public, so visitors could leave notes.
“I was like, ‘Oh, that’s such a great idea,” said Bensky, who is among the Epstein survivors pushing for accountability and justice. “That’ll be so cool to see.”

About a week after the reading room officially opened, Bensky returned and saw “at least six or seven corkboards that were full and overflowing with notes”. There were notes with drawings and notes with abject sadness and “sometimes, it was pure rage”.

“Sometimes, it would be a note directly to a survivor. Sometimes it was a note directly to themselves, and it got everybody involved,” she said. “Even members of survivors’ families were leaving notes. It was just a really beautiful display of our democracy.”
Bensky said the notes have given her hope amid years of institutional failures.

“Being seen in this process has been pretty remarkable.” Visitors have written, “We’re here with you, we stand with you, and we believe you” – demonstrating the “really beautiful empathy that comes with every single note”, Bensky said.

“There have been days where I felt like I couldn’t really do much. I felt really debilitated,” Bensky said. “The reading room can be a lot when you’re walking through your trauma all day, and you’re meeting all kinds of people.

“But so many of us will just go and sit in the room with all the notes and read the notes, and it’s like, ‘Wow, what an extraordinary thing to actually be seen and be believed by so many people at this point.’”
Liz Stein, an Epstein survivor, expressed similar sentiments about the power of these notes.

“It started out with one bulletin board, and I will never forget seeing that one initial bulletin board and just really feeling like, ‘Oh my goodness, people are really reacting to that,’” Stein said. When the first reading room installation ended, these notes “took up the better part of the downstairs of the exhibit”.

“The love that people show us is overwhelming, and every time we do these events with the reading room, every single time, people hug us, they tell us what we mean to them, and a lot of times they’ll say, ‘But it doesn’t matter. I’m just someone you don’t know from somewhere you don’t live,’” Stein said.
“And it’s like, no, we might not know your individual names, but we feel the love.”
“This wall with the note cards is a really tangible visual representation of how much support we have, and that fuels us in a way that I don’t think people quite understand.”
Garrett said that the idea for a notes space came at the last minute. He thought that people might experience deep emotions from the exhibit and might feel the need for support.
body_zh: 一场吸引人们关注爱泼斯坦罪行的巡回演出的参观者留下了数千条“有力”的笔记——幸存者表示这意义重大
当丹妮尔·本斯基第一次去唐纳德·J·特朗普和杰弗里·爱泼斯坦纪念阅览室时，她不知道会发生什么。
“如果我走进去，发现幸存者的名字到处都贴满了，会发生什么？”本斯基对阅览室感到好奇，这是今年五月在纽约市一家画廊首次举办的爱泼斯坦调查档案巡回展览。 “一开始我有点担心这会是对幸存者的一种剥削。
阅览室的目的是让人们关注爱泼斯坦的罪行和执法部门数十年来的不作为。这位前金融家的同事中有许多知名人士，他于 2019 年因性虐待少女而被捕，但在狱中自杀。
虽然吉斯莱恩·麦克斯韦尔因引诱少女进入爱泼斯坦的轨道而被捕并被判有罪，但文件显示，执法官员几十年前就清楚地意识到他们的罪行。幸存者呼吁提高透明度，并对任何其他性虐待参与者采取法律行动。
本斯基也不知道当活动组织者主要事实研究所的创始人大卫·加勒特提出让展览更具互动性的想法时会发生什么。最后一个房间里有一块软木板，加勒特告诉本斯基，当展览向公众开放时，他会将它保留在那里，以便参观者可以留下笔记。
“我当时想，‘哦，这真是个好主意，’本斯基说，他是爱泼斯坦幸存者中推动问责和正义的人之一。 “看到那真是太酷了。”
阅览室正式开放大约一周后，本斯基回来时看到“至少有六七个软木塞满了笔记”。有些笔记上有图画，有些笔记充满了悲惨的悲伤，“有时，这纯粹是愤怒”。
“有时，这是直接写给幸存者的便条。有时，这是直接写给他们自己的便条，它让每个人都参与其中，”她说。 “甚至幸存者家属也留下了笔记。这真是我们民主的美丽展示。”
本斯基表示，在多年的机构失败中，这些笔记给了她希望。
“在这个过程中被看到是非常了不起的。”访客写道：“我们与你同在，我们与你站在一起，我们相信你”——这展示了“每一个音符都蕴含着真正美丽的同理心”，本斯基说。
“有些日子我觉得自己无能为力。我感到非常虚弱，”本斯基说。 “当你一整天都在经历创伤，并且会遇到各种各样的人时，阅览室可能会很拥挤。
“但我们中的很多人只是坐在房间里，拿着所有笔记，阅读笔记，然后就会想，‘哇，在这一点上能被这么多人看到并相信，这是多么了不起的事情啊。’”
爱泼斯坦的幸存者莉兹斯坦对这些笔记的力量表达了类似的看法。
“它是从一个公告板开始的，我永远不会忘记看到那个最初的公告板，我真的感觉，‘哦，天哪，人们真的对此做出了反应，’”斯坦说。当第一个阅览室安装结束时，这些笔记“占据了展览楼下的大部分”。
“人们向我们表达的爱是压倒性的，每次我们在阅览室举办这些活动时，每一次，人们都会拥抱我们，他们告诉我们我们对他们意味着什么，很多时候他们会说，‘但这并不重要。我只是一个你不认识的人，来自你不住的地方，’”斯坦说。
“就像，不，我们可能不知道你们的名字，但我们感受到了爱。”
“这面贴有记事卡的墙是我们拥有多少支持的真正有形的视觉表现，它以一种我认为人们不太理解的方式为我们提供了动力。”
加勒特说，笔记空间的想法是在最后一刻产生的。他认为人们可能会从展览中感受到深刻的情感，并可能感到需要支持。

title_en: Why this GOP governor thinks his party got ‘worse than a butt whipping’ on Tuesday
title_zh: 为什么这位共和党州长认为他的政党周二“比鞭打屁股更糟糕”
summary: Oklahoma Gov. Kevin Stitt blamed the lack of ‘civility’ from President Trump as a reason Republicans got shellacked.
summary_zh: 俄克拉荷马州州长凯文·斯蒂特指责特朗普总统缺乏“礼貌”是共和党遭到猛烈抨击的原因。
body_en: Kevin Stitt, the outgoing Republican governor of Oklahoma, has a message for President Donald Trump: Try being nice.

“People are just kind of tired,” Stitt told POLITICO in an interview Friday morning, three days after the Republican Party suffered devastating election losses across the country and a few hours before Trump elevated Stephen Miller to be his chief of staff.

“They are just ready for something new and a change ... President Trump’s policies are amazing, and he does a really good job on a lot of fronts, but the civility and then just trying to be nice to people, I think would go a long way.”

Stitt, who was until this summer chair of the National Governors Association, has been in Trump’s crosshairs before. In February, Trump lashed out at Stitt in a dispute over the annual NGA gathering at the White House, calling the Oklahoma governor a “ RINO ” and a “ wiseguy .” The two later appeared to patch things up , after a White House sit-down in March.
Stitt is now one of several prominent Republicans calling on the president and congressional leaders to take stock of the party’s midterm losses and change course heading into 2028.
Asked on Friday if Trump had been nice to him, Stitt laughed, before replying: “I’ve always gotten along with President Trump. He’s always been good to me.”

But the term-limited governor, who has said he intends to return to the private sector next year, did not shy away from calling out the president. Stitt urged Trump to stop directing the Department of Justice to go after his political opponents — tactics the governor described as “Third World country stuff” — and use his final two years in the White House to seriously pursue bipartisan immigration reform.
This transcript has been edited for length and clarity.
You called last year’s election results a “ butt whipping ” for the party. If 2025 was a butt whipping, what was 2026?

Oh man! I don't swear, but it's probably worse than a butt whipping. It was pretty bad. But here's the deal: I think it didn't go the way that we had hoped, but I just want everybody to know, it's not the end of the world. We're all Americans, and it really shows you that we're not as partisan as we think. In other words, the American people can swing both directions, right? That’s a positive.
Our leadership matters, the way we conduct ourselves matters. The American people wanted something different, and I think in two years we'll see what happens.
I think [Texas Gov. Greg] Abbott's loss was really the most shocking to me because he's such a good guy and has been a great governor for Texas, and I don't think anybody saw that coming.
What happened? Why do you think the results went the way they did?

People are tired of the self-dealing that they see in politicians. They see people going to Congress and getting rich, and government contracts to big business. I think people are just really, really cranky right now. Obviously, the kitchen table issues like diesel prices are super hard on the average American, and things are costing more, and I think people are frustrated.

We've got to get back to talking about spending. The national debt [is] out of control. We're spending $2 trillion. It doesn't matter if Republicans or Democrats are in office. People don't even talk about tax policy anymore because they think they can spend whatever they want, regardless of income, and that is driving things up.

We have got to have permitting reform done. If you think about why are gas prices so expensive, part of that you could blame on the war in Iran, but a lot of it is the lack of development of new gas processing pipelines. It takes us eight years to build things anymore, and we have so squashed the private sector from meeting the needs of Americans through over-regulation.
Do Republicans need to do a better job of messaging?
They need to do a better job of messaging. But they also need to do a better job of leading when we get there.

I think the American people are so tired of weaponizing the Department of Justice. When President [Joe] Biden, his party was raiding Mar-a-Lago, they were suing President Trump, and then Trump wins big. I wish that we wouldn't have flipped the script and started weaponizing and going after political opponents. This is Third World country stuff. We have got to stop that.

Now, when the Democrats are in power, if they try to start impeaching Trump again and try weaponizing and investigating instead of leading, I think the American people are going to be frustrated in two years again.
body_zh: 即将卸任的俄克拉荷马州共和党州长凯文·斯蒂特向唐纳德·特朗普总统传达了一条信息：尝试表现得友善。
“人们只是有点累了，”斯蒂特周五早上在接受《政治》杂志采访时表示，三天前，共和党在全国范围内遭受了毁灭性的选举失败，而就在特朗普任命斯蒂芬·米勒为幕僚长的几个小时前。
“他们刚刚准备好迎接新的事物和改变……特朗普总统的政策令人惊叹，他在很多方面都做得非常好，但我认为，礼貌以及努力善待人们会大有帮助。”
斯蒂特今年夏天之前一直担任全国州长协会主席，此前一直是特朗普的攻击目标。今年 2 月，特朗普在白宫年度 NGA 聚会的争议中猛烈抨击了斯蒂特，称这位俄克拉荷马州州长为“绿诺”和“智者”。三月份在白宫举行会谈后，两人似乎和解了。
斯蒂特现在是呼吁总统和国会领导人评估该党中期损失并在 2028 年改变路线的几位知名共和党人之一。
周五，当被问及特朗普是否对他很好时，斯蒂特笑了，然后回答道：“我一直和特朗普总统相处得很好。他一直对我很好。”
但这位任期有限的州长表示，他打算明年重返私营部门，他并没有回避对总统的指责。斯蒂特敦促特朗普停止指示司法部追捕他的政治对手——州长称这种策略为“第三世界国家的东西”——并利用他在白宫的最后两年认真推行两党移民改革。
为了篇幅和清晰度，本文字记录已被编辑。
您称去年的选举结果是对该党的“鞭打”。如果 2025 年是一场鞭打，那么 2026 年又是什么？
天啊！我不发誓，但这可能比鞭打屁股更糟糕。情况非常糟糕。但事情是这样的：我认为事情没有像我们希望的那样发展，但我只是想让每个人都知道，这不是世界末日。我们都是美国人，这确实表明我们并不像我们想象的那样有党派之争。换句话说，美国人民可以双向摇摆，对吗？这是积极的。
我们的领导力很重要，我们的行为方式也很重要。美国人民想要一些不同的东西，我想两年后我们就会看到会发生什么。
我认为[德克萨斯州州长格雷格]阿博特的失败对我来说确实是最令人震惊的，因为他是一个非常好的人，并且一直是德克萨斯州一位伟大的州长，我认为没有人预见到这一点。
发生了什么？您认为为什么会出现这样的结果？
人们厌倦了政客的自我交易。他们看到人们进入国会并致富，政府与大企业签订合同。我认为人们现在真的非常非常暴躁。显然，像柴油价格这样的厨房餐桌问题对普通美国人来说非常困难，而且东西的成本越来越高，我认为人们感到沮丧。
我们必须回到谈论支出。国家债务已经失控。我们花费了 2 万亿美元。共和党或民主党执政并不重要。人们甚至不再谈论税收政策，因为他们认为无论收入如何，他们都可以随心所欲地消费，而这正在推动事情的发展。
我们必须进行许可改革。如果你想一想为什么天然气价格如此昂贵，部分原因可以归咎于伊朗战争，但很大程度上是因为缺乏新的天然气加工管道的开发。我们不再需要八年的时间来建造东西，而且我们通过过度监管压制了私营部门满足美国人的需求。
共和党人需要更好地传达信息吗？
他们需要更好地传达信息。但当我们到达那里时，他们还需要更好地领导。
我认为美国人民已经厌倦了将司法部武器化。当拜登总统和他的政党袭击海湖庄园时，他们起诉特朗普总统，然后特朗普大获全胜。我希望我们不会翻转剧本并开始武器化并追捕政治对手。这是第三世界国家的东西。我们必须阻止这种情况。
现在，当民主党掌权时，如果他们试图再次开始弹劾特朗普，并尝试武器化和调查而不是领导，我认为美国人民将在两年内再次感到沮丧。

title_en: Stephen Miller, Trump’s incoming chief of staff, pledges ‘total devotion’ to the president
title_zh: 特朗普即将上任的幕僚长斯蒂芬·米勒承诺“全身心投入”总统
summary: Hardline aide offers ‘unwavering commitment’ to president amid fears White House will double down on far-right immigration agenda Stephen Miller, Donald Trump ’s most controversial aide and the architect of his sweeping immigration crackdown, has lavished prai
summary_zh: 由于担心白宫将在极右翼移民议程上加倍努力，强硬派助手向总统提出“坚定不移的承诺”斯蒂芬·米勒，多纳
body_en: Stephen Miller, Trump’s incoming chief of staff, pledges ‘total devotion’ to the president | Trump administration
Hardline aide offers ‘unwavering commitment’ to president amid fears White House will double down on far-right immigration agenda

Stephen Miller, Donald Trump ’s most controversial aide and the architect of his sweeping immigration crackdown, has lavished praise on the president after his appointment as White House chief of staff.

In his first public remarks since the move was announced, Miller – who begins the role on Monday – pledged “total devotion” to Trump amid concern the administration is now poised to double down on its far-right, nativist immigration agenda.

“If it wasn’t for President Trump the United States of America would not exist right now,” Miller, standing alongside his boss, declared at an event on Friday evening. “This man saved America. He saved our military from collapse. He saved our economy from destruction. He saved our border from annihilation. He saved our country from threats at home and abroad which would have been the end of the American dream for ever.”
Trump’s elevation of Stephen Miller a middle finger to millions of voters

His appointment was unveiled after Americans punished Trump’s Republican party in this week’s US midterm elections, unleashing a blue wave that swept through parts of the country where Democrats have not won in decades.

As of Saturday morning, Republicans have lost seven seats in the Senate, and Democrats hold narrow leads in the two races – Alaska and Mississippi – that have yet to be called. Republicans have also lost 42 seats in the House of Representatives, and five governor races.

Despite this extraordinary array of losses nationwide – which senior Republicans including JD Vance have blamed on the Iran war and tariffs , key pillars of Trump’s agenda – Miller praised the president on Friday for having “saved the Republican party from the ash heap of history and has made it stronger, more popular and more resilient than ever before”.

Miller added: “It is the honor of my life to be President Trump’s chief of staff, and I swear to you, and I pledge to you, Mr President, my absolute loyalty, my unwavering commitment, and my total devotion to your success and the success of this country.”

The speech will likely add to concerns that the Trump administration is set to continue pursuing its hardline immigration agenda, which Miller had been leading in his previous role as deputy chief of staff.

Republicans including longtime Trump ally and adviser Roger Stone and party operative Caroline Wren described Miller as the president’s “wartime consigliere”, drawing a sharp line under Trump’s vague suggestions in recent days that he could seek to work with Democrats after they won back control of the US Congress.

Miller’s appointment has been met with dismay by Democrats and some Republicans, with Marlin Stutzman, the Republican congressman from Indiana, describing the move as a “horrible decision” in comments to Politico .

Don Bacon, the outgoing Republican congressman from Nebraska, predicted that Miller will “have an antagonistic relationship with many”, telling CNN : “He cost us seats in Texas and Arizona by alienating many Hispanic voters who voted for Trump in 2024.”
Miller’s appointment was announced as Trump said he expects to make “a few changes” to his team.
“I love my cabinet. I think they’re good. But I’ll do – be doing maybe a few changes. I don’t want to mention who,” Trump told 60 Minutes , in an interview due to air on Sunday.

Asked if he has confidence in his defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, who has faced questions over his future in the role as the scale of the Republicans’ midterm losses became clear, Trump said “I do”, but notably stopped short of crediting him for what the president said were military successes.
Last month, after reports he might replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff, Trump was unequivocal: there is “zero chance” that will happen, he told reporters.
body_zh: 特朗普即将上任的幕僚长斯蒂芬·米勒承诺“全身心投入”总统|特朗普政府
由于担心白宫将在极右翼移民议程上加倍努力，强硬派助手向总统提出“坚定不移的承诺”
唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)最具争议的助手、全面打击移民行动的策划者史蒂芬·米勒(Stephen Miller)将在共和党在美国中期选举中失去对美国国会的控制权几天后成为他的新任白宫办公厅主任。
米勒周一上任，在此举宣布以来的首次公开讲话中，他承诺“全力支持”特朗普，因为人们担心政府现在准备加倍推行其极右翼、本土主义移民议程。
“如果没有特朗普总统，美利坚合众国现在就不会存在，”米勒站在他的老板旁边，在周五晚上的一次活动中宣称。 “这个人拯救了美国。他拯救了我们的军队免于崩溃。他拯救了我们的经济免遭破坏。他拯救了我们的边境免遭毁灭。他拯救了我们的国家免受国内外的威胁，这将永远是美国梦的终结。”
特朗普向数百万选民竖起中指
他的任命是在美国人在本周的美国中期选举中惩罚了特朗普领导的共和党之后公布的，掀起了一股蓝色浪潮，席卷了民主党几十年来从未获胜的部分地区。
截至周六上午，共和党在参议院失去了七个席位，民主党在阿拉斯加州和密西西比州这两个尚未公布的竞选中以微弱优势领先。共和党还失去了 42 个众议院席位和 5 个州长竞选席位。
尽管全国范围内遭受了一系列非同寻常的损失——包括万斯在内的共和党资深人士将其归咎于伊朗战争和关税，这是特朗普议程的关键支柱——但米勒周五称赞总统“将共和党从历史的垃圾堆中拯救出来，并使其比以往任何时候都更强大、更受欢迎、更有韧性”。
米勒补充道：“成为特朗普总统的幕僚长是我一生的荣幸，我向你发誓，并向你保证，总统先生，我绝对忠诚，我坚定不移的承诺，我将完全奉献给你的成功和这个国家的成功。”
这次演讲可能会加剧人们对特朗普政府将继续推行强硬移民议程的担忧，米勒在担任副幕僚长之前一直领导着这一议程。
特朗普的长期盟友兼顾问罗杰·斯通(Roger Stone)和党内工作人员卡罗琳·雷恩(Caroline Wren)等共和党人将米勒描述为总统的“战时参谋”，这与特朗普最近几天含糊的暗示，即在民主党重新赢得美国国会控制权后，他可能寻求与民主党合作，这与特朗普的“战时参谋”划清了界限。
米勒的任命令民主党人和一些共和党人感到沮丧，来自印第安纳州的共和党国会议员马林·斯塔茨曼在接受《政治》杂志采访时称此举是一个“可怕的决定”。
即将离任的内布拉斯加州共和党议员唐·培根 (Don Bacon) 预测米勒将“与许多人产生敌对关系”，他告诉 CNN：“他疏远了许多在 2024 年投票给特朗普的拉美裔选民，从而让我们失去了德克萨斯州和亚利桑那州的席位。”
米勒的任命是在特朗普表示他希望对他的团队做出“一些改变”时宣布的。
“我爱我的内阁。我认为他们很好。但我会做的——也许会做一些改变。我不想提及是谁，”特朗普在周日播出的《60 分钟》采访中说道。
当被问及他对国防部长皮特·赫格斯是否有信心时，特朗普说“我有信心”，但没有将总统所说的军事成功归功于他。随着共和党中期选举的失败规模变得明朗，他的国防部长皮特·赫格斯的未来面临着质疑。
上个月，在有报道称他可能取代苏西·威尔斯担任白宫办公厅主任后，特朗普对记者明确表示：这种情况发生的“可能性为零”。

title_en: "Forever cruise" arrested at Singapore port, court records show
title_zh: 法庭记录显示“永远的游轮”在新加坡港口被捕
summary: A source familiar with the matter tells CBS News that a fuel supplier likely hired a law firm to pursue legal action against the Odyssey.
summary_zh: 一位知情人士告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，一家燃料供应商可能聘请了一家律师事务所对奥德赛号采取法律行动。
body_en: The Odyssey, the "forever cruise" that has been stranded in Southeast Asia after its owner struggled with financial problems , has been arrested in Singapore, according to court records obtained by CBS News.

A Singaporean law firm, Helmsman LLC, is listed as the arresting solicitor, but it is unclear whom the firm is representing. A source familiar with the matter tells CBS News that it is likely a fuel supplier.
The luxury cruise ship is currently being operated by its lender after its owner, Villa Vie Residences, couldn't keep up with payments.
Villa Vie owes one supplier in the area approximately $500,000, though it's unclear whether that supplier hired the law firm to solicit the arrest.
A ship arrest is a legal process in which a vessel can be detained or seized following a legal claim.
The journey of the MV Odyssey luxury cruise ship, launched in October 2024, came to a sudden end last month in Cambodia, where residents on the ship had just hours to disembark.

title_en: OC fishermen find cruise ship employee treading water miles off coast
title_zh: OC渔民发现游轮员工在离海岸数英里的地方踩水
summary: Two Newport Beach fishermen found a Royal Caribbean cruise ship employee treading water nearly 20 miles off the coast while returning home from a fishing trip near Catalina Island on Friday.
summary_zh: 纽波特海滩的两名渔民发现一名皇家加勒比游轮员工在捕鱼回家途中在离海岸近 20 英里的地方踩水
body_en: Newport Beach fishermen find Royal Caribbean cruise ship employee treading water 20 miles off coast - CBS News
Two Newport Beach fishermen found a Royal Caribbean cruise ship employee treading water nearly 20 miles off the coast while returning home from a fishing trip near Catalina Island on Friday.
Sean Norton and Grant Garrett were fishing for marlin in the morning. By noon, they had rescued the man who had been treading water nearly 20 miles off the coast in the middle of the Pacific Ocean.
"I'm like, 'Yeah, it's a human being. Stop the boat; let's get all of our lines in," Garrett said, recalling the moment the boat's captain spotted the man in the water.
"Grant and I each got an arm and lifted him up," Norton said. "He was in total shock."
Garrett said when the man came to, he told them he was a pianist on the 14-deck Royal Caribbean cruise ship called the "Ovation of the Seas."
"The only thing he said to me was, 'Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,'" Norton said.
After pulling him from the water, the crew put out an emergency maritime call, and a group of Newport Beach lifeguards responded to help.

"It was approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, pretty much in the middle of the ocean," Battalion Chief Adam Yacenda said. They believe he may have gone overboard from the ship about nine hours before he was found, at around 2:30 a.m.

The man, who still hasn't been identified, was hospitalized after the ordeal and is expected to survive, according to the U.S. Coast Guard, which is investigating the incident and how he went overboard.
"You have this crazy super El Niño year. This guy was in the water for probably 10 hours, but the water's 76 degrees," Norton said. "A different year, no way he makes it."

In a statement to CBS LA, a Royal Caribbean Group spokesperson shared, "We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time. To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share."

周五，两名纽波特海滩渔民在卡塔利娜岛附近钓鱼回家时，发现一名皇家加勒比游轮员工在离海岸近 20 英里的地方踩水。
肖恩·诺顿和格兰特·加勒特早上正在钓马林鱼。到了中午，他们救出了这名在距太平洋中部海岸近20英里处涉水的男子。
“我说，‘是的，这是一个人。停下船；让我们把所有的绳索都收进去，’”加勒特回忆起船长在水中发现这个人的那一刻。
“格兰特和我各伸出一只手臂把他举了起来，”诺顿说。 “他完全震惊了。”
加勒特说，当这名男子苏醒过来时，他告诉他们，他是皇家加勒比游轮“海洋赞礼”号 14 层甲板上的一名钢琴家。
“他对我说的唯一一句话就是，‘谢谢你。我以为我要死了，’”诺顿说。
将他从水中救起后，船员们发出了紧急海上呼叫，纽波特海滩的一群救生员也赶来提供帮助。
“它距离海岸约 15 至 20 英里，几乎位于海洋中央，”营长 Adam Yacenda 说。他们认为，他可能在凌晨 2:30 左右被发现，大约九小时后就从船上落水了。
美国海岸警卫队正在调查该事件以及他是如何落水的，据美国海岸警卫队称，这名男子的身份尚未确定，他在经历了磨难后被送往医院，预计会存活下来。
“今年发生了疯狂的超级厄尔尼诺现象。这家伙在水里呆了大概 10 个小时，但水温却高达 76 度，”诺顿说。 “不同的一年，他不可能成功。”
皇家加勒比集团发言人在给哥伦比亚广播公司洛杉矶的一份声明中表示：“在这个困难时期，我们正在向我们的船员提供支持和帮助。为了尊重我们员工的隐私，我们没有更多的细节可以分享。”

body_en: Nov. 8 – Adam Hamilton, Bernie Sanders, Byron Donalds, Josh Shapiro
By Mark Hodge , Amina Kilpatrick and Kayla Hayempour
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said he supports impeachment efforts against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, which are expected to be brought to a vote this week.
Asked in an interview on ABC’s “This Week” whether he would support Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., in his efforts to impeach Hegseth, Jeffries confirmed he supported the push.
“I’m a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution,” Jeffries said.

Jeffries’ support is a major endorsement of the effort and signals how other House Democrats could ultimately vote. The push also tests how far lawmakers are willing to go to oust the top Pentagon official after voters gave low marks to the administration’s handling of the war in Iran, which was a factor in the midterm elections.
Kraków shooting that killed 6 was motivated by far-right views, authorities say
6 killed, 15 injured in shooting at main market square of Krakow, Poland

Poland has declared two days of national mourning after a shooter motivated by far-right ideology killed six people in Kraków on Saturday, in what the country’s defense minister described as a “terror attack.”

The gunman, whom officials described as holding “ultranationalistic” beliefs, reportedly opened fire in the city’s main market square, killing four women and two men. A police officer who confronted him was among the 16 people injured and remains in critical condition.

Polish Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek said the suspect is being investigated on suspicion of murdering six people. He said the attacker “acted with the aim of seriously intimidating a large number of people,” making the shooting a terrorist offense.

The man, who was shot by police and remains in critical condition, is also being investigated in the deaths of three relatives found at his home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, about 93 miles northeast of Kraków.

Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro said he hopes Democrats prioritize healthcare and food assistance when they take control of Congress in January.

“I hope one of the first things that the Congress does is to stop these Medicaid cuts, stop the SNAP cuts, roll back the cuts, the effective cuts in the Affordable Care Act,” Shapiro said in an interview with NBC News’ “Meet the Press.”
“It can’t be either/or,” he said. “It has to be both/and.”
Byron Donalds says GOP needs to take responsibility for the economy to regain trust: Full interview

Florida’s Gov.-elect Byron Donalds, in an exclusive interview with Meet the Press, said “I actually don’t know what” Gov. Ron DeSantis is talking about after DeSantis blamed midterm losses on GOP “gaslighting.”
Asked by moderator Kristen Welker if Republicans should take responsibility for the state of the economy, he said yes.

“If Republicans in my view want to be serious about anything, we have to start having this real political conversation and economic conversation around healthcare to stabilize healthcare costs, lower healthcare costs,” Donalds said.

summary: France says European officials will attend this week's U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, the first three-way round of negotiations since February.
summary_zh: 法国表示，欧洲官员将参加本周在阿布扎比举行的美国斡旋的俄罗斯-乌克兰会谈，这是自去年以来的第一轮三方谈判
body_en: A view through the destroyed walls of a kindergarten shows a large bomb crater and a damaged residential apartment building following a missile attack in Kyiv, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. Dan Bashakov/AP hide caption

European officials will turn up for the U.S.-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine in the United Arab Emirates this week, France's foreign minister said Sunday, days after the Kremlin had insisted there could be no role for European powers at the meeting.

"France will be there and will ensure that Europe's voice is heard," Jean-Noël Barrot told French radio. He did not say who would represent Paris, or whether French or other European officials would take part directly in negotiations, or simply observe.
Melania Trump touts rare agreement she brokered between Russia and Ukraine
The meetings, which are set to take place in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday, had previously been presented as a three-way session between Washington, Moscow and Kyiv.
The Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov had earlier ruled out a European role, saying the trilateral format had already been agreed.

Talking to a Russian news channel on Friday, he accused European governments of failing to decide who speaks for them, while acknowledging that security talks would at some point require Europe's involvement.
On Thursday, President Trump met Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev and said a coming agreement was "going to involve more than Ukraine," adding he could even say it "might involve all of Europe."

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told CNN on Friday that he had not been given details of the agreement Trump had referenced, and warned: "For me, it's not simple, and it can be dangerous." He invoked the 1945 Yalta conference, where Allied leaders settled Europe's division without the involvement of several affected countries.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, right, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attend a press conference in Berlin, Germany, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Ebrahim Noroozi/AP hide caption

This will be the fourth round of talks between the two warring nations brokered by the Trump administration, and the first since those in Geneva this February. Earlier U.S.-brokered meetings have made little progress, and the chances of a breakthrough have been reduced as the Trump administration focused on its war with Iran.

Moscow confirmed it would return to the negotiating table only following a visit by U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg in October. Those talks saw Putin announce the release of an American prisoner from a Russian jail — an apparent Kremlin gesture to President Trump's earlier lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel exports. Ukraine was vehemently opposed to the fuel sales — arguing they helped replenish Moscow's war chest.

Witkoff has said the agenda for these latest talks will include postwar security arrangements and de-escalation of the conflict and humanitarian issues, shortly after Melania Trump helped broker a limited ceasefire that allowed humanitarian aid to enter a town inside Russian-occupied Ukraine.
For Ukraine's Kherson region, a short ceasefire meant a momentary return to normal life

Russia's delegation will again be led by Vladimir Medinsky, a hardline Putin aide who has participated in most talks with Ukraine since the unsuccessful first set of discussions all the way back in March 2022.

For the first time, these talks will also include Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, as well as Yury Zhigarlovsky, a deputy head of the General Staff's operations directorate, alongside military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov.

This more senior lineup could indicate that Moscow is readier than before to address thorny political and military questions. But the U.S. think tankInstitute for the Study of War suggested some of those same Russian officials have in fact previously sought to slow down previous talks or push harder on Moscow's demands.

The gaps between the two countries remain substantial. Russia has demanded that Ukraine give up large parts of its territory and renounce NATO membership. Zelenskyy has repeatedly insisted any security commitments should be clearly spelled out, including who would act, and how, if Russia attacked again.

Russian President Vladimir Putin, right, interacts with people at the monument to merchant Kuzma Minin and Prince Dmitry Pozharsky, leaders of the struggle against foreign invaders in 1612, in Red Square in Moscow, Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, during National Unity Day celebrations. Yuri Kochetkov/Pool Sputnik Kremlin hide caption
body_zh: 2026 年 11 月 7 日星期六，基辅遭受导弹袭击后，透过幼儿园被毁的墙壁可以看到一个大弹坑和一栋受损的住宅公寓楼。Dan Bashakov/美联社隐藏标题栏
法国外交部长周日表示，欧洲官员将于本周出席美国调解的俄罗斯和乌克兰在阿拉伯联合酋长国举行的和平谈判，几天前克里姆林宫坚称欧洲大国不会在会议上发挥作用。
让-诺埃尔·巴罗特对法国电台表示：“法国将出席并确保欧洲的声音被听到。”他没有透露谁将代表巴黎，也没有透露法国或其他欧洲官员是否会直接参与谈判，或者只是旁观。
梅拉尼娅·特朗普吹捧她在俄罗斯和乌克兰之间促成的罕见协议
这些会议定于周二和周三在阿布扎比举行，此前曾被安排为华盛顿、莫斯科和基辅之间的三方会议。
克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫早些时候排除了欧洲的作用，称三边形式已经达成一致。
他周五在接受俄罗斯新闻频道采访时指责欧洲各国政府未能决定谁代表他们，同时承认安全谈判在某些时候需要欧洲的参与。
周四，特朗普总统会见了克里姆林宫特使基里尔·德米特里耶夫，并表示即将达成的协议“将不仅仅涉及乌克兰”，他甚至可以说“可能涉及整个欧洲”。
乌克兰总统泽伦斯基周五告诉美国有线电视新闻网，他没有得到特朗普提到的协议的细节，并警告说：“对我来说，这并不简单，而且可能很危险。”他援引了 1945 年雅尔塔会议，当时盟军领导人在没有几个受影响国家参与的情况下解决了欧洲的分裂问题。
德国总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨（右）和乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基于 2026 年 11 月 3 日星期二在德国柏林出席新闻发布会。Ebrahim Noroozi/美联社隐藏标题栏
这将是特朗普政府斡旋的两个交战国家之间的第四轮会谈，也是自今年二月日内瓦会谈以来的第一轮会谈。早些时候由美国斡旋的会议几乎没有取得任何进展，而且由于特朗普政府专注于与伊朗的战争，取得突破的可能性也降低了。
莫斯科确认，只有在美国特使史蒂夫·威特科夫 (Steve Witkoff) 十月份在圣彼得堡会见俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京 (Vladimir Putin) 后，才会重返谈判桌。在这些会谈中，普京宣布从俄罗斯监狱释放一名美国囚犯——这显然是克里姆林宫对特朗普总统早些时候取消对俄罗斯柴油出口制裁的姿态。乌克兰强烈反对燃料销售，认为这有助于补充莫斯科的战争资金。
威特科夫表示，这些最新会谈的议程将包括战后安全安排以及冲突和人道主义问题的缓和，此前不久，梅拉尼娅·特朗普帮助促成了有限停火，允许人道主义援助进入俄罗斯占领的乌克兰境内的一个城镇。
对于乌克兰赫尔松地区来说，短暂停火意味着暂时恢复正常生活
俄罗斯代表团将再次由普京的强硬助手弗拉基米尔·梅丁斯基(Vladimir Medinsky)率领，自2022年3月第一轮谈判不成功以来，他参加了与乌克兰的大部分会谈。
参加这些会谈的还有副外长谢尔盖·里亚布科夫（Sergei Ryabkov）和米哈伊尔·加卢津（Mikhail Galuzin），以及总参谋部作战局副局长尤里·日加洛夫斯基（Yury Zigarlovsky），以及军事情报局局长伊戈尔·科斯秋科夫（Igor Kostyukov）。
这个更高级的阵容可能表明莫斯科比以前更愿意解决棘手的政治和军事问题。但美国智库战争研究所表示，其中一些俄罗斯官员实际上此前曾试图放慢之前的谈判或更严格地满足莫斯科的要求。
两国之间的差距仍然很大。俄罗斯要求乌克兰放弃大部分领土并放弃北约成员国资格。泽伦斯基一再坚称任何安全承诺都应明确说明，包括如果俄罗斯再次发动袭击，谁将采取行动以及如何采取行动。
2026 年 11 月 4 日星期三，在民族团结日庆祝活动期间，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京（右）在莫斯科红场的商人库兹马·米宁和德米特里·波扎尔斯基王子纪念碑前与人们互动，他们是 1612 年抗击外国侵略者斗争的领导人。尤里·科切特科夫/Pool Sputnik 克里姆林宫 隐藏标题栏

title_en: AP sources: Staff at U.S. center for AI safety are reporting to the White House, raising independence concerns
title_zh: 美联社消息来源：美国人工智能安全中心工作人员正在向白宫汇报，引发独立性担忧
summary: Officials with the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence, or CAISSI, an independent division of the Commerce Department, recently were asked to informally report to an office of the White House.
summary_zh: 超级智能创新与标准推进中心 (CAISSI) 的官员，该中心是商务部的一个独立部门
body_en: Garance Burke, Associated Press Garance Burke, Associated Press
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/staff-at-u-s-center-for-ai-safety-are-reporting-to-the-white-house-raising-independence-concerns

SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — With public anxiety growing over mounting reports about out-of-control artificial intelligence agents, the tiny U.S. government division charged with assessing the safety of new AI offerings lacks a permanent leader and has stopped publishing its research.

Officials with the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence, or CAISSI, an independent division of the Commerce Department, recently were asked to informally report to an office of the White House. That's according to two former government officials with knowledge of the ongoing conversations who spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity to avoid repercussions for current staffers.

The new arrangement concerns some critics, who worry that the executive branch might be politicizing decisions that could affect everything from cybersecurity to bioweapons and that the center's findings could be altered or muted in deference to the tech industry, which has been largely entrusted to police itself.

"These are really powerful institutions that can drastically improve our lives, or the alternative. And the hope is that you can put in nonpartisan or bipartisan technocratic experts to enact policy in a way that best serves the American public," said Caroline Siegel Singh, an AI and emerging technology program manager for the Federation of American Scientists.

Others argue that bringing AI safety officials closer to the orbit of President Donald Trump, who has taken an outwardly hands-off approach to the issue, could give the division more prominence — and perhaps more funding.

The center, which has experienced departures and until recently was called the U.S. Center for AI Standards and Innovation, is allocated $10 million per year. That's about one-eighth the annual budget of its counterpart in the United Kingdom, which is far less celebrated for its frontier technologies.

In April, the division's director was hired and then fired within days. His replacement lasted a few months before he resigned, and the center has been without a permanent leader ever since, although the head of its parent institute doubles as its acting director.

In August, Congress started asking why the center suddenly stopped making public its reports about how safely certain AI systems were performing. San Francisco giant OpenAI also had chimed in by then, asking policymakers to throw more money and support behind the division.

The White House didn't respond to specific questions about CAISSI. But it said in a statement that Trump had formally established his new Super Intelligence Force — the president's preferred term for artificial intelligence. Trump has commissioned a report on risks from his Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, and will ensure "continued U.S. leadership on SI for the benefit of the American people," the White House said.
The federal government often takes an active role in deciding what is safe for the public.

Take the automobile industry, for example. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration sits crash test dummies in cars and then runs them into walls to measure how human bodies are affected by vehicle collisions. Government researchers then analyze the crash test data, share it with the public and prescribe national standards to improve vehicle safety, all with the mission of saving lives and lowering economic costs from crashes.
With AI models, safety testing looks very different.

Under then-President Joe Biden, leading AI companies voluntarily agreed to promote "safe, secure, and transparent development" of their models by sharing details with the newly created division of the Commerce Department and following the administration's guidelines for tests and transparency reports.
WATCH: Trump announces accord signed by top AI companies to 'self-police' development

In September, following alarming reports of AI systems eluding their makers' control, Trump asked leading AI companies to undertake "tremendous self-policing" as part of a voluntary safety pact, but his administration hasn't said how it will monitor the AI companies' implementation.

The technology is advancing so rapidly that many models are now deployed instead as AI agents that work without human prompting and can plan out myriad steps in real-world environments, such as in a recent case in which an AI agent sent a false tip to Philadelphia police about an unsolved homicide case.

As AI capabilities have grown, the government's capacity to independently check these systems hasn't kept pace. There still is no standard process for testing how safely AI agents are acting in the real world, even in simple cases such as when AI agents book a flight, said Sayash Kapoor, an incoming assistant professor at the University of California, Berkeley School of Information.
body_zh: 加兰斯·伯克，美联社 加兰斯·伯克，美联社
旧金山（美联社）——随着公众对越来越多关于失控人工智能代理的报道越来越感到焦虑，负责评估新人工智能产品安全性的美国政府小部门缺乏永久领导者，并已停止发布其研究成果。
美国商务部的一个独立部门——超级智能创新与标准推进中心（CAISSI）的官员最近被要求向白宫办公室进行非正式汇报。据两名了解正在进行的对话的前政府官员透露，他们要求匿名，以避免对现任工作人员造成影响。
新的安排引起了一些批评者的担忧，他们担心行政部门可能会将决定政治化，这些决定可能会影响从网络安全到生物武器的一切，并且该中心的调查结果可能会为了尊重科技行业而被改变或沉默，而科技行业在很大程度上被委托给警察本身。
美国科学家联合会人工智能和新兴技术项目经理卡罗琳·西格尔·辛格（Caroline Siegel Singh）表示：“这些都是非常强大的机构，可以极大地改善我们的生活，或者其他选择。我们希望你可以聘请无党派或两党技术专家，以最有利于美国公众的方式制定政策。”
其他人则认为，让人工智能安全官员更接近唐纳德·特朗普总统的轨道可能会让该部门更加突出，或许还会获得更多资金，而唐纳德·特朗普总统在这个问题上采取了表面上不干涉的态度。
该中心曾经历过退出，直到最近才被称为美国人工智能标准与创新中心，每年拨款 1000 万美元。这大约是英国年度预算的八分之一，而英国的前沿技术远没有那么出名。
4月份，该部门的主管被聘用，但几天之内就被解雇了。在他辞职之前，他的继任者持续了几个月，尽管其上级研究所的负责人兼任代理主任，但从那以后，该中心就一直没有固定的领导者。
八月，国会开始询问为什么该中心突然停止公开有关某些人工智能系统运行安全性的报告。旧金山巨头 OpenAI 当时也插话，要求政策制定者为该部门投入更多资金和支持。
白宫没有回应有关 CAISSI 的具体问题。但它在一份声明中表示，特朗普已经正式建立了他的新超级智能部队——总统对人工智能的首选术语。白宫表示，特朗普已委托其科学技术顾问委员会编写一份有关风险的报告，并将确保“美国在科学技术方面继续发挥领导作用，造福美国人民”。
联邦政府经常在决定什么对公众安全方面发挥积极作用。
以汽车行业为例。美国国家公路交通安全管理局在汽车中放置碰撞测试假人，然后将它们撞到墙上，以测量车辆碰撞对人体的影响。然后，政府研究人员分析碰撞测试数据，与公众分享并制定国家标准以提高车辆安全性，所有这些都旨在挽救生命并降低碰撞造成的经济成本。
有了人工智能模型，安全测试看起来就大不相同了。
在时任总统乔·拜登的领导下，领先的人工智能公司自愿同意通过与商务部新成立的部门分享细节并遵循政府的测试和透明度报告指南来促进其模型的“安全、可靠和透明的开发”。
观看：特朗普宣布顶级人工智能公司签署“自我监管”发展协议
今年 9 月，在有关人工智能系统逃脱制造商控制的令人震惊的报道之后，特朗普要求领先的人工智能公司进行“大规模的自我监管”，作为自愿安全协议的一部分，但他的政府尚未透露将如何监督人工智能公司的实施。
这项技术发展如此之快，以至于现在许多模型都被部署为人工智能代理，它们无需人类提示即可工作，并且可以在现实环境中规划出无数步骤，例如在最近的一个案例中，人工智能代理向费城警方发送了有关未侦破的凶杀案的虚假提示。
随着人工智能能力的增长，政府独立检查这些系统的能力却没有跟上。加州大学伯克利分校信息学院即将上任的助理教授萨亚什·卡普尔 (Sayash Kapoor) 表示，即使在人工智能代理预订航班等简单情况下，仍然没有测试人工智能代理在现实世界中的安全性的标准流程。
